via lactea (noun phrase, first declension + adjective)
latinEntries.meaning: the Milky Way, literally 'the milky road'

definition_zh: 太阳系；太阳与受其引力束缚的全部天体及物质
definition_en: the sun together with all the bodies bound to it by gravity, including the planets, their moons, dwarf planets, asteroids and comets
core_image: 一圈圈同心椭圆围绕中央一颗发亮的黄球，内侧撒着碎石，外侧是带环的巨行星与冰屑带
scene: 博物馆大厅的地板上画着一圈圈同心轨道，中央是一颗发亮的黄球，最外圈散着冰屑。On the museum floor, rings of light trace the solar system around a glowing yellow sun.
sceneCN: 这里 solar system 指「太阳与受其引力束缚的全部天体」（第 1 个义项：以引力范围定义的天文学整体）；句意为地板上的同心光环围绕发亮的黄色太阳，勾出太阳系。图中可辨识物件：地板、同心轨道、黄球、冰屑、参观者的鞋尖。

pos.zh: 太阳系（可数，通常带定冠词 the；复数指别的恒星系统）

collocations.phrase: the formation of the solar system
a model of the solar system

forms.label: 复数
forms.form: solar systems（指其他恒星的行星系统）

senses.title: The sun and everything bound to it
senses.titleCN: 太阳与受其引力束缚的一切
senses.definition: the sun and all the matter held in orbit around it by its gravity
senses.definitionCN: 太阳以及被其引力维持在轨道上的一切物质
senses.example: On the museum floor, rings of light trace the solar system around a glowing yellow sun.
senses.exampleCN: 博物馆地板上，一圈圈光环围绕发亮的黄色太阳，勾出太阳系。
senses.why: the phrase defines the system by its centre: whatever the sun holds becomes part of it, so the boundary is gravitational rather than fixed.
senses.whyCN: 这个短语以中心定义系统：凡被太阳维系者都属其中，因此边界是引力边界而非固定界线。

senses.title: The eight planets and their neighbourhood
senses.titleCN: 八大行星及其中近邻区域
senses.definition: the region containing the eight planets, their moons and the belts of small bodies between and beyond them
senses.definitionCN: 包含八大行星、它们的卫星，以及其间与外侧小天体带的区域
senses.example: The four inner planets of the solar system are rocky and fairly small.
senses.exampleCN: 太阳系的四颗内行星由岩石构成，体积较小。
senses.why: the planets are the largest bound bodies, so the phrase often means their arrangement, even though the system contains far more small debris.
senses.whyCN: 行星是最大的被束缚天体，因此这个短语常指它们的布局，尽管系统中还有远多得多的小碎块。

senses.title: Classes of bodies within it
senses.definition: used to group the objects involved: planets, dwarf planets, moons, asteroids, comets and dust
senses.definitionCN: 用于归类其中的天体：行星、矮行星、卫星、小行星、彗星与尘埃
senses.example: Comets carry frozen material from the outer solar system.
senses.exampleCN: 彗星带着来自太阳系外层的冻结物质。
senses.why: a system is also a set of categories, so textbooks use the phrase as a container for every object class it holds.
senses.whyCN: 系统同时也是一组类别，因此教材用这个短语来容纳其中的每一个天体类别。

senses.title: Its outer boundary
senses.titleCN: 太阳系边界：日球层与奥尔特云
senses.definition: the outer limits marked by the solar wind's bubble and the distant shell of icy bodies
senses.definitionCN: 由太阳风气泡与远处冰质天体壳层标出的外缘
senses.example: Voyager crossed the heliopause, the edge of the solar system's magnetic bubble.
senses.exampleCN: 旅行者号越过了日球层顶，即太阳系磁泡的边缘。
senses.why: since gravity binds bodies far beyond the planets, the phrase needed a practical edge, and the wind's bubble supplied one.
senses.whyCN: 由于引力束缚的天体远在行星之外，这个短语需要一个实用边界，而太阳风气泡提供了它。

senses.title: How it formed
senses.definition: the system as a product of a collapsing cloud of gas and dust about four and a half billion years ago
senses.definitionCN: 约四十五亿年前一团气体与尘埃云坍缩的产物
senses.example: The solar system formed from a disk of dust that later gathered into planets.
senses.exampleCN: 太阳系由一片后来聚成行星的尘埃盘形成。
senses.why: the objects share an age and a composition, so the phrase naturally names a common history rather than only a present arrangement.
senses.whyCN: 这些天体共享同一年龄与成分，因此这个短语自然指一段共同历史，而不只是当下的布局。

senses.title: Other systems by analogy
senses.titleCN: 类比：其他恒星的行星系统
senses.definition: used in the plural for systems of planets around other stars, measured against ours
senses.definitionCN: 用复数指其他恒星周围的行星系统，并以我们的系统为参照
senses.example: Astronomers now compare solar systems around distant stars with our own.
senses.exampleCN: 天文学家如今把远处恒星周围的行星系统与我们的系统相比较。
senses.why: once other planetary systems were found, the familiar phrase became a template, and the plural marks the comparison.
senses.whyCN: 当其他行星系统被发现后，这个熟悉的短语成了模板，复数形式标记的正是这种比较。

senses.title: A person's private centre
senses.titleCN: 比喻：以某人为中心的圈子
senses.definition: figuratively, the circle of people and interests that revolve around one person
senses.definitionCN: 比喻一个人周围旋转的人与事的圈子
senses.example: His office was a small solar system of assistants and messengers.
senses.exampleCN: 他的办公室是一个由助理与信使构成的小小太阳系。
senses.why: the image of bodies circling a centre transfers easily to social life, where one person is the centre others orbit.
senses.whyCN: 天体绕中心的意象很容易转到社交生活：一个人成为中心，别人绕着他转。

senses.title: A model or orrery
senses.definition: a physical or digital model that shows the planets moving around the sun
senses.definitionCN: 展示行星绕太阳运动的实体或数字模型
senses.example: The classroom solar system had brass arms and a lamp for the sun.
senses.exampleCN: 教室里的太阳系模型有黄铜臂，用一盏灯代表太阳。
senses.why: because the real system is too large to see at once, the phrase is also used for the model that stands in for it.
senses.whyCN: 真实的系统大到无法一次看见，因此这个短语也用于替代它的模型。

intro.en: Solar system joins solar, from Latin solaris and sol 'sun', to system, from Greek systema 'an organised whole'. The English phrase is modern, tied to the Copernican view. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: solar system 由 solar 与 system 组合：前者来自拉丁 solaris、sol「太阳」，后者来自希腊 systema「有组织的整体」。这一英语短语属近代说法，与哥白尼体系相关。年代均为约数。

items.en: Latin sol, solis meant 'sun'. Its older Indo-European shape is reconstructed, not recorded, and Greek helios 'sun' is a related but separate form.
items.cn: 拉丁 sol、solis 意为「太阳」。其更早的印欧语形态是重构的，并无记录；希腊 helios「太阳」是相关而独立的形态。

items.en: Solaris 'of the sun' supplied the adjective; English solar came through French and Latin rather than directly from the noun.
items.cn: solaris「太阳的」提供了形容词；英语 solar 经法语与拉丁语而来，并非直接取自名词。

items.en: Greek systema meant 'a whole put together', built on syn- 'together' and histanai 'to set up, stand'.
items.cn: 希腊 systema 意为「组合起来的整体」，由 syn-「一起」与 histanai「安置、站立」构成。

items.en: Latin borrowed systema from Greek, and European languages took it as the ordinary word for an ordered set of parts.
items.cn: 拉丁语从希腊借入 systema，欧洲各语言又把它作为「有序部件集合」的常用词。

items.en: Once the sun rather than the earth was placed at the centre, the phrase solar system became the natural label for the arrangement.
items.cn: 一旦太阳而非地球被置于中心，solar system 便成为描述这一布局的当然名称。

items.en: Source uncertain (first date): the earliest English use of the exact phrase is not firmly dated, and the reconstructed Indo-European form for 'sun' is a hypothesis rather than a recorded word.
items.cn: 来源不确定（首见年代）：这一确切短语最早的英语用例没有可靠年代；表示「太阳」的印欧语重构形式属于假说，并非有记录的词。

note.en: Group one holds phrases built from the same two words or their relatives; group two holds larger or neighbouring astronomical units.
note.cn: 第一组是由这两个词或其同族构成的短语；第二组是更大或相邻的天文单位。

entries.definition: The adjective meaning 'of the sun'; on its own it describes anything sun-related, from panels to storms.
entries.definitionCN: 意为「太阳的」的形容词；单独使用时描述任何与太阳有关的事物，从电池板到风暴。

entries.definition: The general noun for an organised set of parts; outside astronomy it names transport, legal or computer systems.
entries.definitionCN: 泛指有序部件集合的名词；在天文学之外，它指交通、法律或计算机系统。

entries.definition: A system of planets and smaller bodies around a star; it names the planets' side of the arrangement rather than the sun.
entries.definitionCN: 围绕恒星的行星与小天体系统；它强调的是行星一侧，而非太阳。

entries.definition: A small group of stars bound by gravity, such as a binary; the phrase does not require planets at all.
entries.definitionCN: 受引力束缚的小群恒星，如双星；这个短语完全不必有行星。

entries.definition: A system of hundreds of billions of stars; the solar system is one small part of the Milky Way.
entries.definitionCN: 包含数千亿颗恒星的系统；太阳系只是银河系的一小部分。

entries.definition: All matter and space taken together; it contains countless galaxies, so it is not a synonym.
entries.definitionCN: 一切物质与空间的总和；它包含无数星系，因此不是同义词。

entries.definition: The region dominated by the solar wind; it is often treated as the system's practical outer edge.
entries.definitionCN: 由太阳风主导的区域；常被视为太阳系的实用外缘。

entries.definition: The universe seen as an ordered whole, from Greek kosmos; a much wider word than the solar system.
entries.definitionCN: 被视为有序整体的宇宙，来自希腊 kosmos；比太阳系宽泛得多。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real compounds, real astronomy and real morphemes, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的复合词、真实的天文学与真实语素，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: sol 'sun' + -ar, and systema 'organised whole': the sun's organised whole.
normal.cn: sol「太阳」+ -ar，再加 systema「有组织的整体」：太阳的有序整体。

normal.en: The phrase became standard once the sun replaced the earth at the centre.
normal.cn: 当太阳取代地球成为中心，这个短语才成为标准说法。

normal.en: Eight planets, their moons, dwarf planets, asteroids and comets all belong to it.
normal.cn: 八大行星、它们的卫星、矮行星、小行星与彗星都属于它。

normal.en: Its edge is marked by the heliopause, where the solar wind meets interstellar gas.
normal.cn: 它的边缘由日球层顶标出，那里太阳风与星际气体相遇。

normal.en: Plural solar systems compare our arrangement with planets around other stars.
normal.cn: 复数 solar systems 把我们的布局与其他恒星周围的行星相比较。

abstract.en: Picture a lamp in a dark hall with dust specks slowly circling it.
abstract.cn: 想象暗厅里一盏灯，尘埃微粒绕着它慢慢转。

abstract.en: Picture a family tree where every descendant still answers to one ancestor.
abstract.cn: 想象一棵家族树，每个后代都仍听命于同一位祖先。

abstract.en: Picture a stone dropped in still water: rings spread outward from one point.
abstract.cn: 想象一颗石子落进静水：一圈圈涟漪从一点向外散开。

examples.en: Jupiter holds most of the mass of the solar system outside the sun.
examples.cn: 太阳系中除太阳以外的质量，大部分集中在木星。

examples.en: The solar system's outer region is crowded with icy bodies.
examples.cn: 太阳系的外层区域挤满了冰质天体。

examples.en: A simple solar system model shows why inner planets move faster.
examples.cn: 一个简单的太阳系模型就能说明内行星为何运动更快。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「搜了（solar）＋系统（system）」——搜罗太阳管着的一整套天体 → 太阳系

root: 拉丁 sol「太阳」+ 形容词后缀 -aris 构成 solaris，再加希腊 systema「有组织的整体」（syn-「一起」+ histanai「安置」）。英语 solar system 为近代短语。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses start from the gravitational whole, narrow to the planets, widen to object classes and the boundary, then move to its origin, to other stars' systems, to a metaphor and finally to a model.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从引力整体出发，收窄到行星，再扩大到天体类别与边界，随后转向它的起源、别的恒星系统、一个比喻，最后落到模型。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a bright centre with rings of debris circling it at different distances.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个发亮的中心，周围有碎石环在不同距离上绕行。

branches.en: WHOLE AND CORE: the gravitational whole is usually spoken of through its planets.
branches.cn: 整体与核心：引力整体通常通过行星来谈论。

branches.en: CATALOGUE: naming the classes turns the system into an inventory.
branches.cn: 目录：命名各类天体把这个系统变成一份清单。

branches.en: EDGE: the wind's bubble gives the whole a workable border.
branches.cn: 边缘：太阳风气泡给整体一个可用的边界。

branches.en: HISTORY AND ANALOGY: one origin, and then the same phrase applied to other stars.
branches.cn: 历史与类比：一个共同起源，随后同一短语被用于其他恒星。

branches.en: SMALL COPY: a social circle or a classroom model repeats the centre-and-orbits shape.
branches.cn: 缩小的复制：社交圈子或课堂模型重复了「中心与环绕」的形状。

intro.en: The phrase is built from a Latin root for the sun, a Latin adjective suffix, and a Greek noun for an organised whole.
intro.cn: 这个短语由一个表示太阳的拉丁词根、一个拉丁形容词后缀，以及一个表示「有序整体」的希腊名词构成。

latinIntro.en: Latin sol and solaris supply the sun half, and Latin systema, borrowed from Greek, supplies the whole half; the compound itself is modern English.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 sol 与 solaris 提供「太阳」一半，拉丁从希腊借入的 systema 提供「整体」一半；复合本身是近代英语。

items.example: The root also gives solstice and solar.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根还构成 solstice 与 solar。

items.example: Solaris became English solar.
items.exampleCN: solaris 变成英语 solar。

items.example: The prefix survives in system, symmetry and synthesis.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀存留在 system、symmetry 与 synthesis 中。

items.example: Greek systema became Latin systema and English system.
items.exampleCN: 希腊 systema 成为拉丁 systema 与英语 system。

items.example: Solar panels turn light into current.
items.exampleCN: 太阳能板把光变成电流。

items.example: The probe left the solar system's inner region.
items.exampleCN: 探测器离开了太阳系的内层区域。

items.example: Most known planetary systems differ from ours.
items.exampleCN: 已知的行星系统大多与我们的不同。

items.example: The heliosphere shields the planets from cosmic rays.
items.exampleCN: 日球层为行星挡住宇宙射线。

latinEntries.structure: systema, systematis (n., third declension; borrowed from Greek)

definition_zh: 太阳的；太阳能的；由太阳产生的；太阳神经丛的；（诗）阳光般的
definition_en: relating to the sun, or powered by its light and heat
core_image: 一排深蓝色板面朝南铺在屋顶，正午光落在上面，细电线把电流引到屋内
scene: 屋顶上一排深蓝色板面朝向南方，正午的阳光落在上面，电线一直通到屋内的电池。Rows of dark blue panels on the roof turn solar radiation into electricity.
sceneCN: 这里 solar 指「由太阳产生的」（第 3 个义项：用于太阳辐射、太阳风、日食等由太阳产生的现象）；句意为屋顶上成排的深蓝板面把太阳辐射转成电。图中可辨识物件：屋顶、深蓝板面、正午光斑、电缆、屋内电池。

pos.zh: 太阳的；太阳能的；由太阳产生的；（解剖）太阳神经丛的；（诗）阳光般的

forms.label: 比较级
forms.form: more solar（罕用，关系形容词通常不比较）

senses.title: Of or relating to the sun
senses.definition: relating to the sun as an object, its structure or its position
senses.definitionCN: 指作为天体的太阳、其结构或位置的
senses.example: Solar physics studies the sun's interior and atmosphere.
senses.exampleCN: 太阳物理学研究太阳的内部与大气。
senses.why: the adjective is a straight derivative of the Latin noun for the sun, so its oldest job is simply to attach 'sun' to another noun.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词直接由拉丁语「太阳」名词派生，因此最古老的功能就是把「太阳」挂到另一个名词上。

senses.title: Powered by sunlight
senses.titleCN: 太阳能的、靠阳光供能的
senses.definition: using light or heat from the sun as an energy source
senses.definitionCN: 以太阳的光或热作为能源
senses.example: The village runs its pumps on solar power.
senses.exampleCN: 这个村子用太阳能电力驱动水泵。
senses.why: as panels and cells became common, the adjective shifted from 'belonging to the sun' to 'working on the sun's energy'.
senses.whyCN: 随着电池板与电池普及，这个形容词从「属于太阳的」转为「靠太阳能工作的」。

senses.title: Caused by the sun
senses.definition: used of events produced by the sun, such as eclipses, flares, wind and radiation
senses.definitionCN: 用于太阳造成的事件，如日食、耀斑、太阳风与辐射
senses.example: Rows of dark blue panels on the roof turn solar radiation into electricity.
senses.exampleCN: 屋顶上成排的深蓝板面把太阳辐射转成电。
senses.why: in these compounds the sun is the cause rather than the owner, which is why the same adjective covers both a solar eclipse and a solar panel.
senses.whyCN: 在这些复合词中，太阳是原因而非所有者；正因此，同一个形容词既管日食，也管太阳能板。

senses.title: Measured by the sun
senses.titleCN: 按太阳计量的时间与历法
senses.definition: used of timekeeping based on the sun, as in a solar day, a solar year or a solar calendar
senses.definitionCN: 用于以太阳为准的计时，如太阳日、太阳年或阳历
senses.example: A solar year is slightly longer than three hundred and sixty-five days.
senses.exampleCN: 一个太阳年比三百六十五天稍长。
senses.why: the sun's apparent motion is the oldest clock, so the adjective marks any unit defined by that motion rather than by the moon.
senses.whyCN: 太阳的视运动是最古老的钟，因此这个形容词标记一切由该运动而非月亮定义的单位。

senses.title: Passive solar design
senses.definition: used of building methods that collect or exclude sunlight without pumps or panels
senses.definitionCN: 指不靠水泵或电池板、直接采集或遮挡阳光的建筑做法
senses.example: Passive solar design keeps the house warm without extra fuel.
senses.exampleCN: 被动式太阳能设计让房子不用额外燃料也保持温暖。
senses.why: architecture borrowed the adjective to name a design that uses the sun's geometry directly, with no machine in between.
senses.whyCN: 建筑学借用这个形容词，命名一种直接利用太阳几何关系、中间不隔机器的设计。

senses.title: The solar plexus
senses.titleCN: 解剖学中的太阳神经丛
senses.definition: used in the fixed term solar plexus for the network of nerves behind the stomach
senses.definitionCN: 用于固定术语 solar plexus，指胃后方的神经网
senses.example: A blow to the solar plexus knocks the wind out of a person.
senses.exampleCN: 打在太阳神经丛上会让人一时喘不上气。
senses.why: anatomists saw radiating nerve fibres and named them after the sun's rays, so the adjective here is a metaphor frozen into a term.
senses.whyCN: 解剖学家看到辐射状的神经纤维，便以太阳光线命名；此处的形容词是一个凝固为术语的比喻。

senses.title: Poetic: sunny, radiant
senses.titleCN: 诗体用法：阳光般的、明亮的
senses.definition: in older or poetic writing, bright and warm like the sun
senses.definitionCN: 在较古或诗意文字中，指像太阳一样明亮温暖的
senses.example: The poet praised her solar smile in an age of formal praise.
senses.exampleCN: 在崇尚正式颂辞的年代，诗人赞美她阳光般的笑容。
senses.why: before the word was technical it was simply descriptive, and that older warmth survives in literary use.
senses.whyCN: 在这个词变得技术化之前，它只是描述性的；那份古老的暖意仍存留在文学用法里。

senses.title: Solar deity and astrology
senses.definition: used of a god identified with the sun, or of a chart's sun sign and solar return
senses.definitionCN: 指与太阳等同的神，或占星中的太阳星座与太阳返照
senses.example: Roman religion honoured a solar deity alongside household gods.
senses.exampleCN: 罗马宗教在家庭神之外也敬奉一位太阳神。
senses.why: worship and astrology both treat the sun as a power with a personality, so they keep the adjective in its oldest, personal sense.
senses.whyCN: 崇拜与占星都把太阳当作有人格的力量，因此它们保留了这个形容词最古老、人格化的用法。

intro.en: Solar comes from Latin solaris 'of the sun', from sol, solis 'sun'. The Latin noun's deeper Indo-European shape is reconstructed. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: solar 来自拉丁 solaris「太阳的」，源头是 sol、solis「太阳」。这个拉丁名词更早的印欧语形态属重构。年代均为约数。

items.en: Sol was the ordinary Latin word for the sun and also the name of the sun god; the two uses were not separated.
items.cn: sol 是拉丁语中「太阳」的常用词，也是太阳神的名字；两种用法并未分开。

items.en: Solaris 'of the sun' was formed with the adjective suffix -alis, giving the stem that English would borrow.
items.cn: solaris「太阳的」由形容词后缀 -alis 构成，提供了英语后来借用的词干。

items.en: Sol also combined with sistere 'to stand still' in solstitium, the sun's standing point, which gives English solstice.
items.cn: sol 还与 sistere「停住」结合成 solstitium，即太阳停驻之点，由此有了英语 solstice。

items.en: English took solar from Latin in the Middle English period, first in astronomical and calendrical writing.
items.cn: 英语在中古英语时期从拉丁语借入 solar，最早用于天文与历法文字。

items.en: From the nineteenth century solar spread into engineering and medicine: solar engine, solar plexus, solar cell.
items.cn: 从 19 世纪起，solar 扩展到工程与医学：太阳能发动机、太阳神经丛、太阳能电池。

items.en: Source uncertain (deeper origin): the pre-Latin history of sol is not recorded, and the Indo-European form usually cited is a reconstruction; its link to Greek helios is a family resemblance, not a direct borrowing.
items.cn: 来源不确定（更深词源）：sol 在拉丁语之前的历史没有记录，通常引用的印欧形式属于重构；它与希腊 helios 的联系是同族相似，而非直接借入。

note.en: Group one holds words that look related to sol; group two holds adjectives that describe sunlight without sharing the root.
note.cn: 第一组是看上去与 sol 有关的词；第二组是描述阳光但不共享词根的形容词。

entries.definition: Sol plus sistere 'to stand': the day the sun seems to stop, so it shares the root but names a date, not the sun.
entries.definitionCN: sol 加 sistere「停住」：太阳看似停驻的那一天；共享词根，但指日期而非太阳。

entries.definition: A Latin-derived word for a room or bed used for sun treatment; it keeps the root but adds a place suffix.
entries.definitionCN: 源自拉丁的词，指用于日光治疗的房间或床；保留词根，加上表示场所的后缀。

entries.definition: In- 'in' plus sol plus -ation: the amount of solar radiation reaching a surface, a technical measure rather than the sun itself.
entries.definitionCN: in-「进入」加 sol 加 -ation：到达某一表面的太阳辐射量，是技术量而非太阳本身。

entries.definition: The musical syllable sol comes from a medieval hymn to John the Baptist, not from the Latin sun; the two words are homographs only.
entries.definitionCN: 音乐唱名 sol 来自中世纪一首施洗约翰赞美诗，与拉丁「太阳」无关；两词只是同形异源。

entries.definition: Full of sunshine or cheerful in mood; it describes conditions and people, while solar names causes and systems.
entries.definitionCN: 阳光充足或心情开朗；描述天气与人，而 solar 指原因与系统。

entries.definition: Actually reached by sunlight, as a sunlit wall; it is a result word, not a relational one.
entries.definitionCN: 真正被阳光照到的，如被阳光照亮的墙；它描述结果，而非关系。

entries.definition: From Greek helios 'sun', used of a star rising with the sun; it marks the Greek branch of the same family.
entries.definitionCN: 来自希腊 helios「太阳」，指与太阳同时升起的恒星；它标记同一词族的希腊分支。

entries.definition: Belonging to the sky in general, from Latin caelum; solar is one narrow slice of the celestial.
entries.definitionCN: 泛指属于天空，来自拉丁 caelum；solar 只是其中很窄的一片。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real compounds and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Latin sol 'sun' + -ar: the plain adjective of the sun.
normal.cn: 拉丁 sol「太阳」+ -ar：太阳的普通形容词。

normal.en: sol + sistere 'stand' gave solstice, the day the sun stands still.
normal.cn: sol 加 sistere「停住」给出 solstice，即太阳停驻的那一天。

normal.en: Fixed compounds carry the modern senses: solar energy, solar wind, solar eclipse.
normal.cn: 固定搭配承载现代义：太阳能、太阳风、日食。

normal.en: The Greek branch of the family appears in helios and heliacal.
normal.cn: 词族的希腊分支出现在 helios 与 heliacal 中。

normal.en: The frozen metaphor solar plexus names nerves that spread like rays.
normal.cn: 凝固的比喻 solar plexus 命名了像光线一样散开的神经。

abstract.en: Picture a single lamp that can heat a room, charge a battery and set the calendar.
abstract.cn: 想象一盏灯，既能暖屋、充电，又能定历法。

abstract.en: Picture a sunflower turning its face to follow a moving point of light.
abstract.cn: 想象一朵向日葵转脸追随一个移动的光点。

abstract.en: Picture a net of nerves drawn as rays from one bright centre.
abstract.cn: 想象一张神经网从明亮的中心呈放射状画出。

examples.en: Solar panels on the school roof supply most of its electricity.
examples.cn: 学校屋顶的太阳能板提供其大部分电力。

examples.en: A total solar eclipse darkened the town for nearly three minutes.
examples.cn: 一次日全食让全镇暗了将近三分钟。

examples.en: The solar year is the basis of the calendar we use.
examples.cn: 太阳年是我们所用历法的基础。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「索拉（solar）」——向天上索要拉下一束光 → 太阳的、太阳能的

root: 拉丁 sol、solis「太阳」+ 形容词后缀 -aris → solaris → 英语 solar；同一词根加 sistere「停住」构成 solstitium，即英语 solstice。sol 更深来源不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses radiate from one centre: the sun as an object, then its energy, its effects, its clock, its architecture, a nerve net named after rays, a poetic glow and finally a god.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从一个中心辐射出去：作为天体的太阳、它的能量、它造成的现象、它当钟表、它在建筑中的用法、以光线命名的神经网、诗意的光辉，最后是一位神。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a single bright source whose light and heat reach everything around it.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个明亮源头，其光与热到达周围一切。

branches.en: SOURCE: the sun is both the object studied and the cause of what happens.
branches.cn: 源头：太阳既是被研究的对象，也是所发生之事的原因。

branches.en: USE: panels and passive design turn the source into a supply.
branches.cn: 利用：电池板与被动式设计把源头变成供给。

branches.en: CLOCK: the sun's motion defines the day and the year.
branches.cn: 钟表：太阳的运动定义了日与年。

branches.en: RAYS AS IMAGE: nerves and smiles borrow the look of sunlight.
branches.cn: 光线作意象：神经与笑容借用了阳光的样子。

branches.en: A POWER WITH A FACE: worship and astrology keep the personal sense.
branches.cn: 有面孔的力量：崇拜与占星保留了人格化的义。

intro.en: Solar is a Latin root plus a Latin adjective suffix, and the same root builds several English words through different suffixes.
intro.cn: solar 是一个拉丁词根加拉丁形容词后缀，同一词根通过不同后缀构成若干英语词。

latinIntro.en: Latin sol 'sun' yields solaris, solstitium and solarium; the root is also visible in the technical term insolation.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 sol「太阳」衍生 solaris、solstitium 与 solarium；这个词根也见于技术术语 insolation。

items.example: The root is the same in solstice and solarium.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根在 solstice 与 solarium 中相同。

items.meaning: belonging to; of the kind of
items.example: Solaris became the English adjective solar.
items.exampleCN: solaris 成为英语形容词 solar。

items.example: The summer solstice is the longest day.
items.exampleCN: 夏至是一年中最长的一天。

items.example: Patients rested in the solarium each morning.
items.exampleCN: 病人每天上午在日光室里休息。

items.meaning: sun exposure received by a surface
items.example: Insolation peaks at midday.
items.exampleCN: 日照量在正午达到峰值。

items.example: Solar radiation warms the upper soil.
items.exampleCN: 太阳辐射温暖表层土壤。

items.example: A solar-powered pump lifts water to the field.
items.exampleCN: 一台太阳能水泵把水提到田里。

items.example: Solstitial storms arrive with the turn of the year.
items.exampleCN: 至日风暴随年岁的转折到来。

items.meaning: of a star rising with the sun
items.example: The heliacal rising of Sirius marked the flood season.
items.exampleCN: 天狼星的偕日升标记了洪水季。

definition_zh: 行星的；行星系统的；地球整体的；行星齿轮的
definition_en: relating to a planet or planets, or to a whole planet as a single system
core_image: 一颗带环的行星被投影放大到整面穹顶，环的影子斜斜落在球面上
scene: 天文馆把一颗带环的行星放大投到整面穹顶，环的影子斜斜落在球面上。A projector throws a planetary image across the whole dome.
sceneCN: 这里 planetary 指「行星的」（第 1 个义项：与行星有关的）；句意为投影仪把一幅行星图像铺满整个穹顶。图中可辨识物件：穹顶、带环行星、环影、投影仪、座椅。

pos.zh: 行星的；行星系统的；全球整体的；（机械）行星齿轮的

collocations.zh: 行星边界（地球系统的安全界限）

forms.label: 比较级
forms.form: more planetary（罕用，关系形容词通常不比较）

senses.title: Of a planet
senses.definition: relating to a planet as a body, its surface, interior or motion
senses.definitionCN: 指作为天体的行星及其表面、内部或运动
senses.example: A projector throws a planetary image across the whole dome.
senses.exampleCN: 投影仪把一幅行星图像铺满整个穹顶。
senses.why: the adjective was built from planet plus the Latin suffix -arius, so its base job is to attach 'planet' to another noun.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词由 planet 加拉丁后缀 -arius 构成，基本功能就是把「行星」挂到另一个名词上。

senses.title: Of a planetary system
senses.definition: relating to a system of planets and smaller bodies around a star
senses.definitionCN: 指围绕恒星的行星与小天体系统
senses.example: Planetary systems seem to be common in our galaxy.
senses.exampleCN: 行星系统在我们的星系中似乎很常见。
senses.why: once planets were known to come in systems, the adjective covered the whole arrangement rather than one body.
senses.whyCN: 当人们知道行星成系统出现后，这个形容词便覆盖整个布局，而不只一个天体。

senses.title: Planetary nebula, a misnomer
senses.titleCN: 行星状星云：一个历史误称
senses.definition: used in the fixed term planetary nebula for a shell of gas thrown off by a dying star, so named because it looked like a planet's disk
senses.definitionCN: 用于固定术语「行星状星云」，指垂死恒星抛出的气体壳，得名于它像行星的圆盘
senses.example: The Ring Nebula is a planetary nebula, not a planet at all.
senses.exampleCN: 环状星云是一个行星状星云，根本不是行星。
senses.why: early telescopes showed a round disk, so observers guessed 'planet'; the name stuck even after the object was understood as gas.
senses.whyCN: 早期望远镜只看到一个圆盘，观测者便猜是行星；即使后来弄清它是气体，名字仍留了下来。

senses.title: Planetary gears
senses.definition: used of a gear set in which smaller gears revolve around a central one, like planets around a sun
senses.definitionCN: 指小齿轮绕中央齿轮旋转的齿轮组，形似行星绕日
senses.example: A planetary gear set changes speed within a small housing.
senses.exampleCN: 行星齿轮组在很小的壳体内改变转速。
senses.why: engineers borrowed the astronomical picture because the motion is literally the same: several bodies circling one centre.
senses.whyCN: 工程师借用了天文学的图景，因为运动确实相同：几个体绕一个中心转。

senses.title: Planet-wide, as one system
senses.titleCN: 全球整体的、整个行星尺度的
senses.definition: relating to an entire planet treated as one system, especially the earth's climate and limits
senses.definitionCN: 把整个行星当作一个系统来看，尤指地球气候与其界限
senses.example: Climate change is a planetary problem that no single state can solve.
senses.exampleCN: 气候变化是一个任何单一国家都无法解决的行星级问题。
senses.why: earth science needed a word for processes that operate across the whole globe, and 'planetary' supplied it without adding a new root.
senses.whyCN: 地球科学需要一个词来描述遍及整个地球的过程，而 planetary 无需另造词根就提供了它。

senses.title: Astrological planetary hours
senses.definition: used in astrology for hours or rulers assigned to the seven traditional planets
senses.definitionCN: 占星中把时段或主宰者分配给七颗传统行星的用法
senses.example: Old almanacs listed a planetary ruler for each hour of the day.
senses.exampleCN: 旧历书为一天中的每个时辰列出主宰行星。
senses.why: astrology kept the older seven-planet scheme, so the adjective still carries a meaning that astronomy has dropped.
senses.whyCN: 占星保留了旧的七行星体系，因此这个形容词仍带有一层天文学已弃用的含义。

senses.title: Disciplines of planetary study
senses.titleCN: 行星研究各学科的用法
senses.definition: used in names of fields such as planetary geology, planetary atmospheres and planetary protection
senses.definitionCN: 用于行星地质学、行星大气、行星保护等学科名称
senses.example: Planetary geology compares volcanoes on earth and on Venus.
senses.exampleCN: 行星地质学比较地球与金星上的火山。
senses.why: each field studies the same class of object by a different method, so the adjective serves as the common label in their titles.
senses.whyCN: 各领域用不同方法研究同一类天体，因此这个形容词成为它们名称中的共同标签。

senses.title: Enormous, planet-sized
senses.definition: used loosely for something of enormous size or reach, as if it covered a planet
senses.definitionCN: 口语中形容某事物极其巨大或影响极广，仿佛覆盖整个行星
senses.example: The delay was a planetary embarrassment for the agency.
senses.exampleCN: 这次延误对该机构而言是一场行星级的难堪。
senses.why: the adjective can be exaggerated because a planet is a unit everyone can picture, so it works as hyperbole outside science.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词可以夸张使用，因为行星是人人都能想象的单位，于是它在科学之外成了夸张语。

intro.en: Planetary joins Greek planētēs 'wanderer', used of the moving stars, to the Latin adjective suffix -arius. The word first entered English through astrology and astronomy. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: planetary 由希腊 planētēs「漫游者」与拉丁形容词后缀 -arius 组合而成；planētēs 原指会移动的星。这个词最早经占星与天文进入英语。年代均为约数。

items.en: Greek planētēs meant 'wanderer', from planasthai 'to wander'; the moving points of light were 'wandering stars' as opposed to fixed ones.
items.cn: 希腊 planētēs 意为「漫游者」，来自 planasthai「漫游」；会移动的光点被称为「游星」，以区别于恒星。

items.en: The verb planasthai 'to wander, roam' is the source of the noun; its own earlier history is not established.
items.cn: 动词 planasthai「漫游、游荡」是该名词的来源；它自身更早的历史尚未确定。

items.en: Latin took the Greek noun as planeta, still meaning a wandering star, and passed it to the European languages.
items.cn: 拉丁语把希腊名词借作 planeta，仍指游星，并把它传给欧洲各语言。

items.en: The suffix -arius formed adjectives of belonging, as in planetarius 'of the planets', also used for an astrologer.
items.cn: 后缀 -arius 构成表示归属的形容词，如 planetarius「行星的」，也用来指占星者。

items.en: English planetary appears in the seventeenth century as the telescope turned wandering lights into worlds.
items.cn: 英语 planetary 出现在 17 世纪，正值望远镜把游动的光点变成一个个世界。

items.en: Source uncertain (first date and deeper origin): no exact first citation is firmly dated for the adjective, and the pre-Greek origin of planasthai remains unsettled.
items.cn: 来源不确定（首见年代与更深词源）：这个形容词没有确切可靠的最早书证；planasthai 在希腊语之前的来源亦无定论。

note.en: Group one holds words built on the same planet stem; group two holds adjectives of scale that overlap in use.
note.cn: 第一组是同出 planet 词干的词；第二组是用法上有重叠的尺度类形容词。

entries.definition: The body itself, from Greek 'wanderer'; the adjective adds relation, not a new object.
entries.definitionCN: 天体本身，来自希腊「漫游者」；形容词只是加上关系，不指新的对象。

entries.definition: A small body that accretes into planets; it shares the stem but adds -esimal 'small particle'.
entries.definitionCN: 聚合成行星的小天体；共享词干，加 -esimal「小颗粒」。

entries.definition: An asteroid-sized body, literally 'planet-shaped'; it is not a planet and takes a different suffix.
entries.definitionCN: 小行星大小的天体，字面「行星状的」；它不是行星，且用了不同后缀。

entries.definition: Inter- 'between' plus planetary: the space or travel between planets, not a property of one.
entries.definitionCN: inter-「之间」加 planetary：行星之间的空间或航行，而非某一颗行星的属性。

entries.definition: Covering the whole earth, from globe; it overlaps planetary in climate talk but names the earth only.
entries.definitionCN: 覆盖整个地球，来自 globe；在气候话题中与 planetary 重叠，但只指地球。

entries.definition: Of the earth or its land, from Latin terra; it contrasts with planetary when planets other than earth are meant.
entries.definitionCN: 属于地球或陆地的，来自拉丁 terra；当指地球以外的行星时，它便与 planetary 相对。

entries.definition: Relating to an orbit rather than to the planet itself; planetary motion is described, but orbital names the track.
entries.definitionCN: 与轨道而非行星本身有关；行星运动会用到它，但它命名的是轨迹。

entries.definition: Belonging to the sky in general; planetary is one category within the celestial.
entries.definitionCN: 泛指属于天空；planetary 只是天空中的一类。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real compounds, real relatives and real etymology, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的搭配、真实同族词与真实词源，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Greek planētēs 'wanderer': the planets were the stars that wandered.
normal.cn: 希腊 planētēs「漫游者」：行星就是会漫游的星。

normal.en: The family runs planet, planets, planetary, planetesimal, planetoid, interplanetary.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 planet、planets、planetary、planetesimal、planetoid、interplanetary。

normal.en: Fixed terms mark each field: planetary science, planetary nebula, planetary gear.
normal.cn: 固定术语标出各领域：行星科学、行星状星云、行星齿轮。

normal.en: Planetary nebula is a misnomer: it is gas, named for looking like a disk.
normal.cn: 行星状星云是误称：它是气体，得名于看起来像圆盘。

normal.en: Planetary gears copy the same motion: small wheels around a centre.
normal.cn: 行星齿轮复制同一运动：小轮绕中心转。

abstract.en: Picture seven bright dots that refuse to stay in their places.
abstract.cn: 想象七个不肯待在原位的亮点。

abstract.en: Picture a single round room containing every climate and every coast.
abstract.cn: 想象一个圆房间，装下所有气候与所有海岸。

abstract.en: Picture a small wheel circling a larger one inside a watch case.
abstract.cn: 想象表壳里一只小轮绕着大轮转。

examples.en: Planetary scientists compare the atmospheres of Venus and Mars.
examples.cn: 行星科学家比较金星与火星的大气。

examples.en: The planetary nebula glows because a dying star shed its outer layers.
examples.cn: 行星状星云发光，是因为一颗垂死恒星抛掉了外层。

examples.en: Water use has crossed a planetary boundary in several regions.
examples.cn: 在若干地区，用水已越过了行星边界。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「普拉内（planet）」——天上那颗到处乱跑的星 → 行星的

root: 希腊 planētēs「漫游者」来自 planasthai「漫游」，经拉丁 planeta 进入欧洲语言；加拉丁后缀 -arius 成 planetarius，即英语 planetary。planasthai 更深来源不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses move from one planet to a system of them, then to a misnamed gas shell and a gear set, then to the whole earth, to astrology, to named disciplines and finally to plain exaggeration.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从一颗行星走到行星系统，再走到被误称的气体壳与齿轮组，然后到整个地球、占星、各学科名称，最后到纯粹的夸张。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a round body with a ring, standing for everything that circles a centre.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个带环的圆体，代表一切绕中心转的东西。

branches.en: BODY AND SET: one planet, then the arrangement it belongs to.
branches.cn: 天体与集合：先是一颗行星，再是它所属的布局。

branches.en: CIRCLING SHAPE: a gas shell and a gear train both borrow the round, orbiting look.
branches.cn: 环绕之形：气体壳与齿轮组都借用了圆形、绕行的外观。

branches.en: THE WHOLE AS ONE: earth processes and whole disciplines are named by the same adjective.
branches.cn: 整体为一：地球过程与整门学科都用同一个形容词命名。

branches.en: OLD SCHEME: astrology keeps the seven-planet meaning that astronomy dropped.
branches.cn: 旧体系：占星保留了天文学已弃用的七行星含义。

branches.en: BORROWED UNIT: a planet becomes a figure of speech for anything huge.
branches.cn: 借来的单位：行星成了形容任何巨大事物的修辞。

intro.en: Planetary is the noun planet plus the Latin suffix -arius; the stem also builds several scientific words with different suffixes.
intro.cn: planetary 是名词 planet 加拉丁后缀 -arius；同一词干还用不同后缀构成若干科学词。

latinIntro.en: Latin planeta 'wandering star' and planetarius 'of the planets' carry the Greek root into English; the suffix -arius also gives -ary in English.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 planeta「游星」与 planetarius「行星的」把希腊词根带入英语；后缀 -arius 在英语中作 -ary。

items.example: The root calls the planets wandering stars.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根把行星称作游星。

items.example: Planetarius became English planetary.
items.exampleCN: planetarius 成为英语 planetary。

items.example: Mars is the fourth planet from the sun.
items.exampleCN: 火星是离太阳第四颗行星。

items.example: The outer planets are mostly gas.
items.exampleCN: 外行星主要由气体构成。

items.example: Planetary images filled the dome.
items.exampleCN: 行星图像铺满了穹顶。

items.example: Planetesimals collided and grew.
items.exampleCN: 星子碰撞并长大。

items.example: Ceres was once called a planetoid.
items.exampleCN: 谷神星曾被称为小行星体。

items.example: Interplanetary dust grains hit the probe.
items.exampleCN: 行星际尘埃颗粒撞上探测器。

items.example: The first exoplanet was found in nineteen ninety-five.
items.exampleCN: 第一颗系外行星于一九九五年被发现。

latinEntries.structure: planeta, planetae (m., first declension; from Greek)
planetarius, planetaria, planetarium (adj., first and second declension)
latinEntries.meaning: of the planets; also a noun for an astrologer
latinEntries.meaningCN: 行星的；亦作名词指占星者

latinEntries.meaning: a device or place showing planetary motion
latinEntries.meaningCN: 演示行星运动的装置或场所

definition_zh: 行星；地球（作为人类家园时的指称）；（占星）行星（含日月）
definition_en: a large round body that orbits a star and has cleared its own path of smaller debris, or such a body in general speech
core_image: 望远镜目镜里一颗带条纹的圆球悬在黑色背景中，旁边有一条细细的光环
scene: 望远镜前，一颗带条纹的圆球悬在黑色背景里，旁边有一条细细的光环。A single planet hangs in the eyepiece, striped and ringed.
sceneCN: 这里 planet 指「绕恒星运行、近似球形并清空轨道附近的大天体」（第 1 个义项：天文学的定义）；句意为目镜中悬着一颗有条纹、带环的行星。图中可辨识物件：目镜筒、带条纹圆球、细光环、黑色背景、支架。

pos.zh: 行星；地球；占星意义上的行星（含日月）

collocations.zh: 绕其他恒星运行的行星

senses.title: The IAU definition
senses.titleCN: 天文学定义：绕恒星、近似球形、清空轨道
senses.definition: a body that orbits the sun or another star, is massive enough to be nearly round, and has cleared its neighbourhood of comparable bodies
senses.definitionCN: 绕太阳或其他恒星运行、质量足以近似球形，并已清空轨道附近同类天体的天体
senses.example: A single planet hangs in the eyepiece, striped and ringed.
senses.exampleCN: 目镜中悬着一颗有条纹、带环的行星。
senses.why: the definition was tightened in 2006 to separate planets from the many similar-sized bodies in belts, so three conditions replaced the older informal one.
senses.whyCN: 这一定义在 2006 年被收紧，以把行星与带中大量同样大小的天体区分开，于是三条条件取代了旧的松散说法。

senses.title: One of the eight
senses.definition: one of the eight bodies recognised in the solar system, from Mercury to Neptune
senses.definitionCN: 太阳系中公认的八颗天体之一，从水星到海王星
senses.example: Jupiter is the largest planet in the solar system.
senses.exampleCN: 木星是太阳系中最大的行星。
senses.why: everyday use keeps the older, simpler list, so 'planet' usually means one of the eight even in careful speech.
senses.whyCN: 日常用法沿用更旧、更简单的名单，因此即使在谨慎的说法里，planet 通常也指八颗之一。

senses.title: A planet of another star
senses.titleCN: 其他恒星的行星（系外行星）
senses.definition: used with modifiers for bodies orbiting stars other than the sun
senses.definitionCN: 与修饰语连用，指绕太阳以外恒星运行的天体
senses.example: The telescope found a planet in a tight four-day orbit.
senses.exampleCN: 望远镜发现了一颗四天就绕一圈的行星。
senses.why: once other stars were known to have such bodies, the noun needed no new word; the modifier carries the difference.
senses.whyCN: 当其他恒星被确认拥有这类天体后，这个名词无需新词，差别由修饰语承担。

senses.title: Dwarf planet as a boundary case
senses.definition: used in the compound dwarf planet for a round body that has not cleared its neighbourhood, such as Pluto
senses.definitionCN: 用于复合词「矮行星」，指近似球形但未清空轨道附近的天体，如冥王星
senses.example: Pluto was reclassified as a dwarf planet in 2006.
senses.exampleCN: 冥王星在 2006 年被改归为矮行星。
senses.why: the boundary had to be drawn somewhere, and the compound keeps the old word while marking the failed third condition.
senses.whyCN: 边界总得画在某处，而这个复合词保留了旧词，同时标出它未满足第三条条件。

senses.title: The earth as 'the planet'
senses.definition: used with the definite article to mean the earth, especially in environmental talk
senses.definitionCN: 带定冠词时指地球，尤用于环境话题
senses.example: We treat the planet as if its resources had no limit.
senses.exampleCN: 我们把这颗行星当作资源没有上限。
senses.why: seen from outside, the earth is simply one planet, so the definite noun becomes a way of speaking about all of us at once.
senses.whyCN: 从外面看，地球只是一颗行星，因此这个带冠词的名词成了一种把所有人一起谈论的说法。

senses.title: Living on another planet
senses.titleCN: 比喻：心不在焉、脱离现实
senses.definition: in the phrase on another planet, describing someone out of touch with present reality
senses.definitionCN: 用于短语「在另一颗行星上」，形容某人心不在焉、脱离现实
senses.example: His plan was elegant and completely on another planet.
senses.exampleCN: 他的方案很精巧，却完全不接地气。
senses.why: the image works because another planet is a place with different rules, so a person out of touch seems to live there.
senses.whyCN: 这个意象成立，是因为另一颗行星是一个规则不同的地方，脱离现实的人仿佛就住在那儿。

senses.title: Astrology's seven planets
senses.titleCN: 占星中的七行星（含日月）
senses.definition: in astrology, one of the seven traditional bodies: sun, moon, Mercury, Venus, Mars, Jupiter and Saturn
senses.definitionCN: 占星中七颗传统天体之一：日、月、水星、金星、火星、木星与土星
senses.example: Old charts assign each planet a day of the week.
senses.exampleCN: 旧星盘为每颗行星分配一周中的一天。
senses.why: astrology preserves the ancient list in which the sun and moon also wandered, so its 'planets' are not the astronomer's.
senses.whyCN: 占星保留了太阳与月亮也会游走的古老名单，因此它的「行星」并非天文学家的行星。

senses.title: The old wandering stars
senses.definition: historically, any of the lights that moved against the fixed stars, including the sun and moon
senses.definitionCN: 历史上指任何相对于恒星移动的光点，包括太阳与月亮
senses.example: Ancient observers counted seven planets, sun and moon included.
senses.exampleCN: 古代观测者数出七颗行星，日月也在其中。
senses.why: the word meant 'wanderer' before it meant 'world', so the older list follows the original meaning rather than the modern one.
senses.whyCN: 这个词在指「世界」之前意为「漫游者」，因此旧的名单遵循原义而非今义。

senses.title: A world in fiction
senses.titleCN: 虚构作品中的「行星世界」
senses.definition: used in science fiction for a habitable or visited world with its own conditions
senses.definitionCN: 在科幻作品中指可居住或可造访、有自身条件的世界
senses.example: The crew landed on a planet where a day lasts a month.
senses.exampleCN: 船员降落在一颗一天长达一个月的行星上。
senses.why: stories need a unit of setting larger than a country and smaller than a galaxy, and the planet supplies exactly that.
senses.whyCN: 故事需要一个大于国家、小于星系的设定单位，而行星恰好提供了它。

intro.en: Planet comes from Greek planētēs 'wanderer', through Latin planeta and Old French. The word meant a moving star long before it meant a world. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: planet 来自希腊 planētēs「漫游者」，经拉丁 planeta 与古法语进入英语。在它指「世界」之前，很久以来都指会移动的星。年代均为约数。

items.en: Greek astronomers called the five moving lights planētēs, 'wanderers', because they drifted against the fixed stars.
items.cn: 希腊天文学家把五个移动的光点称作 planētēs「漫游者」，因为它们相对恒星漂移。

items.en: Latin borrowed the noun as planeta and kept the meaning 'wandering star'; the sun and moon were often counted among them.
items.cn: 拉丁语借作 planeta，保留「游星」之义；太阳与月亮常被算在其中。

items.en: Old French planete carried the word into English in the Middle Ages, still as an astronomical body rather than a world.
items.cn: 古法语 planete 在中世纪把这个词带入英语，仍指天文天体而非一个世界。

items.en: From the seventeenth century telescopes showed planets as disks and worlds, and the word shifted from 'moving light' to 'physical body'.
items.cn: 从 17 世纪起，望远镜让行星显出圆盘与世界的模样，这个词便从「移动的光」转为「实体天体」。

items.en: The International Astronomical Union fixed three conditions in 2006 and created the dwarf planet category for bodies that fail the third.
items.cn: 国际天文学联合会在 2006 年定下三条条件，并为未满足第三条的天体设立「矮行星」类别。

items.en: Source uncertain (deeper origin): the pre-Greek history of planasthai 'to wander' is not established, and any older Indo-European form proposed for it is a reconstruction.
items.cn: 来源不确定（更深词源）：planasthai「漫游」在希腊语之前的历史没有定论，凡为其提出的更早印欧形式均属重构。

note.en: Group one holds words derived from planet that name related bodies; group two holds sky objects that are often mistaken for planets.
note.cn: 第一组是由 planet 派生、指相关天体的词；第二组是常被误认作行星的天空对象。

entries.definition: The adjective of planet; it describes relations and systems rather than naming a body.
entries.definitionCN: planet 的形容词；描述关系与系统，而非命名天体。

entries.definition: A small body that looks like a planet but is not one; the -oid suffix marks resemblance, not membership.
entries.definitionCN: 形似行星而非行星的小天体；-oid 后缀标记相似而非归类。

entries.definition: One of the small bodies that collide and grow into planets; it is a stage, not a category of planet.
entries.definitionCN: 碰撞并长成行星的小天体之一；它是一个阶段，而非行星的一个类别。

entries.definition: Exo- 'outside' plus planet: a planet of a star other than the sun, so the head noun is still planet.
entries.definitionCN: exo-「在外」加 planet：太阳以外某颗恒星的行星，中心词仍是 planet。

entries.definition: A body that shines by its own fusion; planets only reflect light, which is why the two were once distinguished by motion.
entries.definitionCN: 靠自身核聚变发光的天体；行星只反射光，这正是两词最初靠运动来区分的原因。

entries.definition: A natural body orbiting a planet; a planet orbits a star, so the two words mark different centres.
entries.definitionCN: 绕行星运行的天然天体；行星绕恒星，因此两词标记不同的中心。

entries.definition: A place with its own conditions, often used for planets in fiction; it is a broader, older word.
entries.definitionCN: 有自身条件的地方，常用于虚构中的行星；是更宽、更古老的词。

entries.definition: The neutral word for any discrete object in space, used when the class is unknown or unimportant.
entries.definitionCN: 指太空中任何独立天体的中性词，用于类别未知或不重要时。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real compounds, real relatives and real history, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的搭配、真实同族词与真实历史，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Greek planētēs 'wanderer': planets were the lights that wandered.
normal.cn: 希腊 planētēs「漫游者」：行星就是会漫游的光点。

normal.en: The family runs planet, planets, planetary, planetoid, planetesimal, exoplanet.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 planet、planets、planetary、planetoid、planetesimal、exoplanet。

normal.en: Three IAU conditions: orbit a star, be nearly round, clear the neighbourhood.
normal.cn: 国际天文学联合会三条条件：绕恒星、近似球形、清空轨道附近。

normal.en: The eight are Mercury, Venus, Earth, Mars, Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus, Neptune.
normal.cn: 八颗是水星、金星、地球、火星、木星、土星、天王星、海王星。

normal.en: Astrology still counts sun and moon among its seven planets.
normal.cn: 占星仍把太阳与月亮算在它的七颗行星中。

abstract.en: Picture a marble circling a lamp in a dark room.
abstract.cn: 想象暗室里一颗弹珠绕着一盏灯转。

abstract.en: Picture a single room that must hold everyone's weather at once.
abstract.cn: 想象一个房间必须同时装下所有人的天气。

abstract.en: Picture a stranger who follows rules from a place nobody else can see.
abstract.cn: 想象一个按别人看不见的地方的规则行事的陌生人。

examples.en: Mercury is the smallest planet and the closest to the sun.
examples.cn: 水星是最小的行星，也是离太阳最近的一颗。

examples.en: Planets form from the same disk of dust that makes their star.
examples.cn: 行星由构成其恒星的同一片尘埃盘形成。

examples.en: The probe will study the planet's thin atmosphere from orbit.
examples.cn: 探测器将在轨道上研究这颗行星的稀薄大气。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「普拉内特（planet）」——天上到处乱跑的那颗球 → 行星

root: 希腊 planētēs「漫游者」← planasthai「漫游」，经拉丁 planeta、古法语 planete 进入英语；今义经望远镜观测由「移动的光」转为「实体世界」。planasthai 更深来源不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses begin with the tightened definition, move to the eight, to other stars' planets and the dwarf boundary, then to the earth itself, a metaphor, astrology, the old list and fiction.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项先从收紧后的定义开始，再到八颗行星、别的恒星的行星与矮行星边界，然后到地球本身、一个比喻、占星、旧名单与虚构作品。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one round body held in a path around a much larger light.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个圆体被维持在一条绕更大光源的路径上。

branches.en: DEFINITION AND LIST: a strict rule and the familiar eight answer the same question at different depths.
branches.cn: 定义与名单：严格规则与熟悉的八颗在不同深度回答同一个问题。

branches.en: EDGES OF THE CLASS: other stars' planets and dwarf planets test where the word stops.
branches.cn: 类别的边缘：别恒星的行星与矮行星都在试探这个词的边界。

branches.en: ONE PLANET, TWO VIEWS: the earth as home, and a metaphor for being out of touch.
branches.cn: 一颗行星两种看法：作为家园的地球，以及脱离现实的比喻。

branches.en: OLD LISTS: astrology and ancient astronomy keep sun and moon inside the word.
branches.cn: 旧名单：占星与古代天文学把日月留在词内。

branches.en: STAGE OF A STORY: fiction uses the planet as its unit of setting.
branches.cn: 故事的舞台：虚构作品把行星当作设定单位。

intro.en: Planet is a Greek noun borrowed through Latin; English builds a large family from it with suffixes for relation, resemblance and size.
intro.cn: planet 是经拉丁借入的希腊名词；英语用表示关系、相似与大小的后缀从中构建了一个大词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin planeta and the adjective planetarius carry the word; Latin also said stella errans 'wandering star' for the same object.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 planeta 与形容词 planetarius 承载这个词；拉丁也用 stella errans「游星」指同一对象。

items.example: The Greek word named the moving lights.
items.exampleCN: 这个希腊词命名了会移动的光点。

items.example: Latin kept the astronomical sense.
items.exampleCN: 拉丁语保留了天文学义。

items.example: The planet has a four-day year.
items.exampleCN: 这颗行星的一年只有四天。

items.example: The eight planets differ greatly in size.
items.exampleCN: 八大行星大小差异极大。

items.example: Planetary science grew from telescope work.
items.exampleCN: 行星科学由望远镜工作发展而来。

items.example: The planetoid orbits between Mars and Jupiter.
items.exampleCN: 这个小行星体在火星与木星之间运行。

items.example: Planetesimals stuck together in the early disk.
items.exampleCN: 早期盘中星子粘合在一起。

items.example: Thousands of exoplanets are now known.
items.exampleCN: 现已知道数千颗系外行星。

items.example: Interplanetary travel remains slow.
items.exampleCN: 行星际旅行仍然缓慢。

latinEntries.structure: planeta, planetae (m., first declension; from Greek)
stella errans (noun phrase, first declension + present participle)
planetarius, planetaria, planetarium (adj., first and second declension)

definition_zh: 行星轨道；行星绕恒星或航天器绕行星运行的路径
definition_en: the path followed by a planet around a star, or by a spacecraft around a planet, usually an ellipse
core_image: 墙上挂图里一圈被压扁的椭圆绕着一盏灯，椭圆上标出两个焦点与一条短轴
scene: 教室墙上的图里，一颗小球沿一圈压扁的椭圆绕中央的灯运行，椭圆上标着两个焦点。A thin ellipse on the chart traces the planetary orbit around the lamp at its focus.
sceneCN: 这里 planetary orbit 指「行星绕恒星运行的路径」（第 1 个义项：以椭圆为主的轨道）；句意为图上一条细椭圆画出绕焦点处那盏灯的 planetary orbit。图中可辨识物件：挂图、压扁的椭圆、焦点标记、中央灯、小球。

pos.zh: 行星轨道（可数；复数指多条轨道或不同行星的轨道）

collocations.zh: 绕恒星的多条行星轨道

senses.title: The path around a star
senses.definition: the continuous path a planet follows around its star, close to an ellipse with the star at one focus
senses.definitionCN: 行星绕恒星运行的连续路径，近似椭圆，恒星位于其中一个焦点
senses.example: A thin ellipse on the chart traces the planetary orbit around the lamp at its focus.
senses.exampleCN: 图上一条细椭圆画出绕焦点处那盏灯的行星轨道。
senses.why: the path is fixed by gravity and by the planet's speed, so the phrase names the resulting curve rather than the motion itself.
senses.whyCN: 路径由引力与行星速度共同决定，因此这个短语命名的是结果曲线，而非运动本身。

senses.title: Orbital elements
senses.titleCN: 轨道要素：半长轴、偏心率、倾角
senses.definition: the set of numbers that fixes an orbit: size, shape, tilt and direction
senses.definitionCN: 确定一条轨道的一组数值：大小、形状、倾斜与朝向
senses.example: Six orbital elements are enough to describe a planetary orbit.
senses.exampleCN: 六个轨道要素就足以描述一条行星轨道。
senses.why: once a path is treated as a curve in space, it can be reduced to measurable parameters, which is why the phrase appears in tables of numbers.
senses.whyCN: 一旦路径被视为空间中的曲线，就可以化为一组可测参数，因此这个短语常出现在数值表里。

senses.title: Period and Kepler's laws
senses.titleCN: 轨道周期与开普勒定律
senses.definition: the timing of one complete circuit, tied to distance by Kepler's third law
senses.definitionCN: 绕行一整圈的时间，并由开普勒第三定律与距离相联系
senses.example: A wider planetary orbit always takes longer to complete.
senses.exampleCN: 更宽的行星轨道总是需要更长时间走完一圈。
senses.why: the orbit is also a clock: the same curve that fixes position fixes the length of the year.
senses.whyCN: 轨道同时也是一只钟：确定位置的同一条曲线也确定了「一年」的长度。

senses.title: Resonance and perturbation
senses.definition: the slow changes produced when planets pull on one another, including locked rhythms called resonances
senses.definitionCN: 行星相互牵引造成的缓慢变化，包括被锁定的节律即共振
senses.example: Two neighbouring planets settled into a stable orbital resonance.
senses.exampleCN: 两颗相邻行星进入了稳定的轨道共振。
senses.why: no orbit is perfectly alone, so the phrase also covers the small deviations that neighbouring bodies impose over long periods.
senses.whyCN: 没有一条轨道是完全孤立的，因此这个短语也涵盖邻近天体在长时间里造成的小偏差。

senses.title: Tilt against the ecliptic
senses.definition: the angle at which a planetary orbit stands relative to the plane of the earth's orbit
senses.definitionCN: 一条行星轨道相对于地球轨道平面所成的角度
senses.example: Pluto's planetary orbit is tilted well away from the ecliptic.
senses.exampleCN: 冥王星的行星轨道明显偏离黄道面。
senses.why: orbits lie at different angles, so the phrase often needs a reference plane to say how far one is tilted.
senses.whyCN: 各轨道处在不同角度上，因此这个短语常需要一个参考平面来说明倾斜多少。

senses.title: Planetary migration
senses.definition: the change of a planet's orbit over time as it interacts with gas, dust or other bodies
senses.definitionCN: 行星与气体、尘埃或其他天体相互作用时轨道随时间发生的变化
senses.example: Models show the giant's planetary orbit migrating inward early on.
senses.exampleCN: 模型显示这颗巨行星的行星轨道在早期向内迁移。
senses.why: an orbit is stable only in the short run, so the phrase also names a history: the path was once elsewhere.
senses.whyCN: 轨道只在短期稳定，因此这个短语也命名一段历史：这条路径曾经在别处。

senses.title: Predicting positions
senses.definition: used in ephemeris work, where the path allows astronomers to forecast where a planet will appear
senses.definitionCN: 用于星历表工作，凭轨道可预测行星将在何处出现
senses.example: Navigation tables relied on a precise planetary orbit for Mars.
senses.exampleCN: 导航表依赖一条精确的火星行星轨道。
senses.why: a calculated path is a forecast, which is why the phrase appears in almanacs and navigation long before spaceflight.
senses.whyCN: 一条算出的路径就是一份预报，因此这个短语早在航天之前就出现在历书与航海表中。

senses.title: A spacecraft's orbit at a planet
senses.titleCN: 航天器绕行星运行的轨道
senses.definition: the path of a spacecraft around a planet, reached by a manoeuvre called orbit insertion
senses.definitionCN: 航天器绕行星运行的路径，通过称为「入轨」的机动抵达
senses.example: The probe entered a low planetary orbit after a six-month cruise.
senses.exampleCN: 探测器在半年巡航后进入低行星轨道。
senses.why: engineers reused the phrase because the geometry is identical: a small body circling a large one.
senses.whyCN: 工程师沿用了这个短语，因为几何关系完全相同：小天体绕大天体。

intro.en: Planetary orbit joins planetary, from Greek planētēs 'wanderer', to orbit, from Latin orbita 'wheel-rut, track'. The phrase belongs to modern astronomy. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: planetary orbit 由 planetary（源自希腊 planētēs「漫游者」）与 orbit（源自拉丁 orbita「车辙、轨迹」）组合而成。这个短语属近代天文学。年代均为约数。

items.en: Orbita meant the rut left by a wheel and, by extension, any circular track; it comes from orbis 'circle, disk'.
items.cn: orbita 指车轮留下的辙，引申为任何圆形轨迹；它来自 orbis「圆、盘」。

items.en: Orbis named a circle or a disk, and also the round world; its deeper origin is not established.
items.cn: orbis 指圆或盘，也指圆形的世界；其更深来源尚未确定。

items.en: English orbit first meant the eye socket and the path of a heavenly body, both from the idea of a track.
items.cn: 英语 orbit 最初既指眼窝，也指天体路径，两者都出自「轨迹」这一想法。

items.en: Kepler's work on elliptical paths made orbit the standard word for a closed path around a centre.
items.cn: 开普勒关于椭圆路径的工作使 orbit 成为指绕中心闭合路径的标准词。

items.en: Planetary orbit became a fixed phrase as astronomers compared the paths of planets with those of comets and moons.
items.cn: 当天文学家把行星路径与彗星、卫星路径相比较时，planetary orbit 成为固定短语。

items.en: Source uncertain (first date and deeper origin): the earliest use of the exact phrase is not firmly dated, and the pre-Latin origin of orbis is unsettled, so older forms offered for it are reconstructions.
items.cn: 来源不确定（首见年代与更深词源）：这一确切短语的最早用例没有可靠年代；orbis 在拉丁语之前的来源亦无定论，凡为其给出的更早形式均属重构。

note.en: Group one holds the orbit family that is constantly interchanged; group two holds words for a path or a circuit.
note.cn: 第一组是常被互换使用的 orbit 词族；第二组是表示路径或一圈的词。

entries.definition: The path itself, of any body around any other; planetary orbit only narrows the class of bodies.
entries.definitionCN: 任何天体绕任何天体的路径；planetary orbit 只是限定了天体的类别。

entries.definition: An adjective of orbit, but also a noun in chemistry for an electron's probability region; the second use is unrelated to planets.
entries.definitionCN: orbit 的形容词，但化学中也作名词指电子出现的概率区域；后一用法与行星无关。

entries.definition: The duration of one circuit; it measures the orbit in time rather than in space.
entries.definitionCN: 绕行一圈的时长；它从时间而非空间上度量轨道。

entries.definition: The flat surface containing an orbit; a path is a curve, while the plane is the sheet it lies in.
entries.definitionCN: 包含轨道的平面；路径是曲线，而平面是它所在的纸面。

entries.definition: The path of a moving object, especially one not repeating, from Latin 'to throw across'; orbits repeat, trajectories often do not.
entries.definitionCN: 运动物体的路径，尤指不重复的路径，来自拉丁「横抛」；轨道会重复，轨迹常常不重复。

entries.definition: The plain word for a route; it says nothing about gravity or closure.
entries.definitionCN: 表示路线的日常词；不涉及引力或闭合。

entries.definition: One complete turn around a centre; it names the act of circling rather than the curve.
entries.definitionCN: 绕中心完整转一圈；它指绕行的动作，而非曲线本身。

entries.definition: The closed oval curve that most orbits approximate; it is the geometry, not the physical motion.
entries.definitionCN: 多数轨道近似的闭合椭圆曲线；它是几何形状，而非物理运动。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real terms, real relatives and real etymology, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实术语、真实同族词与真实词源，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Latin orbita 'wheel-rut': an orbit is a track worn in space.
normal.cn: 拉丁 orbita「车辙」：轨道就是空间里磨出的辙。

normal.en: Six orbital elements fix an orbit: size, shape, tilt and direction.
normal.cn: 六个轨道要素确定一条轨道：大小、形状、倾斜与方向。

normal.en: Kepler's third law ties a wider orbit to a longer year.
normal.cn: 开普勒第三定律把更宽的轨道与更长的一年绑在一起。

normal.en: The family runs orbit, orbital, orbiting, orbital period, orbit insertion.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 orbit、orbital、orbiting、orbital period、orbit insertion。

normal.en: Planetary orbits are ellipses with the star at one focus.
normal.cn: 行星轨道是椭圆，恒星位于其中一个焦点。

abstract.en: Picture a groove worn in a field by a cart going round and round.
abstract.cn: 想象一辆车在田野里绕圈，磨出一道沟。

abstract.en: Picture two dancers who never touch but cannot leave each other's rhythm.
abstract.cn: 想象两个舞者从不触碰，却离不开对方的节拍。

abstract.en: Picture a train whose timetable is fixed by the shape of its rails.
abstract.cn: 想象一列火车，时刻表由轨道的形状决定。

examples.en: The comet crosses the planetary orbits of Mars and Jupiter.
examples.cn: 这颗彗星穿过火星与木星的行星轨道。

examples.en: A planetary orbit can be read as a record of past gravitational pulls.
examples.cn: 一条行星轨道可读作过去引力牵引的记录。

examples.en: The spacecraft needed a burn to reach a stable planetary orbit.
examples.cn: 航天器需要一次点火才能进入稳定的行星轨道。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「普拉内（plane）＋ orbit（轨道）」——行星走的那条椭圆跑道 → 行星轨道

root: planetary 源自希腊 planētēs「漫游者」；orbit 源自拉丁 orbita「车辙、轨迹」，其源 orbis 为「圆、盘」。两词合为近代天文学短语。orbis 更深来源不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow a curve outward: the path itself, its numbers, its clock, its wobbles, its tilt, its history, its forecasts and finally a spacecraft using it.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿一条曲线展开：路径本身、它的数值、它的钟、它的摆动、它的倾斜、它的历史、它的预报，最后是借用它的航天器。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a flattened ellipse drawn around a lamp, with the lamp at one focus.
core.cn: 核心意象：一条绕灯的扁椭圆，灯位于其中一个焦点。

branches.en: CURVE AND COORDINATES: a drawn path becomes a set of numbers.
branches.cn: 曲线与坐标：画出的路径变成一组数值。

branches.en: SPACE AND TIME: the same curve fixes both a position and a year, and its tilt fixes a plane.
branches.cn: 空间与时间：同一条曲线既定位置也定一年，而倾角定出一个平面。

branches.en: UNSTABLE OVER LONG SPANS: pulls and migration mean the path has a history.
branches.cn: 长时段的不稳定：牵引与迁移意味着这条路径有历史。

branches.en: FORECAST: a known path predicts where a planet will be.
branches.cn: 预报：已知路径能预测行星将在何处。

branches.en: REUSED GEOMETRY: a probe around a planet copies the same circle.
branches.cn: 复用的几何：绕行星的探测器复制了同一个圆。

intro.en: The phrase is transparent: a Greek-derived adjective naming the body, plus a Latin-derived noun naming the track.
intro.cn: 这个短语是透明的：希腊来源的形容词命名天体，拉丁来源的名词命名轨迹。

latinIntro.en: Latin orbita and orbis supply the track half; Greek planētēs supplies the body half through Latin planeta.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 orbita 与 orbis 提供「轨迹」一半；希腊 planētēs 经拉丁 planeta 提供「天体」一半。

items.example: The Latin word pictured a groove, not a circle.

items.meaning: a closed path around a centre

items.example: Orbital speed falls with distance.

items.example: An orbiting telescope avoids the lower air.
items.exampleCN: 在轨望远镜避开了低层大气。

items.example: Planetary orbits differ in tilt.

definition_zh: 轨道；绕行；（影响、势力）范围；眼窝；原子轨道
definition_en: the curved path of one body around another, or to move along such a path
core_image: 孩子甩着一根系绳的小球，小球绕着握绳的手一圈圈转，绳在空气里拉出圆的痕迹
scene: 操场边的孩子把一只系绳的小球甩起来，小球绕着握绳的手一圈圈转。The child lets the ball swing in a wide orbit around one hand.
sceneCN: 这里 orbit 指「一个物体绕另一个物体运行的路径」（第 1 个义项：绕行的曲线路径）；句意为孩子让小球绕着一只手划出宽宽的轨道。图中可辨识物件：系绳小球、握绳的手、圆形痕迹、操场地面、孩子背影。

pos.zh: 轨道；势力范围；眼窝；（物理）原子轨道
绕……运行；沿轨道飞行

senses.title: A path around a body
senses.definition: the curved path of a body around a more massive one under gravity
senses.definitionCN: 在引力作用下，一个天体绕更大质量天体的弯曲路径
senses.example: The child lets the ball swing in a wide orbit around one hand.
senses.exampleCN: 孩子让小球绕着一只手划出宽宽的轨道。
senses.why: the word began as the rut of a wheel, so the earliest idea is a track that something follows rather than a force that pulls it.
senses.whyCN: 这个词最初指车轮的辙，因此最早的想法是某物沿着走的轨迹，而非拉着它的力。

senses.title: To move along that path
senses.definition: to travel around a body in a closed or repeating path
senses.definitionCN: 沿闭合或重复的路径绕某天体运行
senses.example: The station orbits the earth once every ninety minutes.
senses.exampleCN: 空间站每九十分钟绕地球一圈。
senses.why: once the noun meant a track, the verb could mean travelling on it, and English formed it without adding any new root.
senses.whyCN: 既然名词意为轨迹，动词自然可意为沿轨迹行进，英语无需另加词根就构成了它。

senses.title: One complete circuit
senses.definition: one completed trip around a body, used as a unit of time or counting
senses.definitionCN: 绕某天体完整走完的一圈，用作计时或计数的单位
senses.example: The satellite completed its thousandth orbit this morning.
senses.exampleCN: 这颗卫星今早完成了第千圈绕行。
senses.why: a closed path can be counted, so the same noun measures repetition rather than only geometry.
senses.whyCN: 闭合路径可以计数，因此同一个名词也度量重复次数，而不只度量几何。

senses.title: An electron's orbital
senses.titleCN: 物理与化学中的原子轨道
senses.definition: in physics and chemistry, a region where an electron is likely to be found around a nucleus
senses.definitionCN: 物理与化学中指电子在核周围出现的概率区域
senses.example: The first shell holds one spherical orbital.
senses.exampleCN: 第一层只有一个球形轨道。
senses.why: early models pictured electrons circling like planets, and the word survived after the picture became a probability cloud.
senses.whyCN: 早期模型把电子想成像行星一样绕行，而在这个图像变成概率云之后，这个词仍留了下来。

senses.title: The eye socket
senses.definition: the bony cavity that holds the eye
senses.definitionCN: 容纳眼球的骨质腔
senses.example: A blow near the orbit can damage the eye itself.
senses.exampleCN: 眼窝附近的打击可能伤到眼睛本身。
senses.why: the socket is a ring-shaped hollow, and Latin used the same wheel-track word for it, so English kept both senses.
senses.whyCN: 眼窝是环形的凹处，拉丁语用同一个「车辙」词指它，因此英语保留了两义。

senses.title: A sphere of influence
senses.definition: the range within which a person, country or idea exerts influence
senses.definitionCN: 一个人、国家或观念施加影响的范围
senses.example: Smaller states moved into the larger neighbour's orbit.
senses.exampleCN: 较小的国家进入了更大邻国的影响圈。
senses.why: bodies near a massive one are held by it, so politics borrowed the picture for clients held by a power.
senses.whyCN: 靠近大质量天体的物体会被它牵住，因此政治借这幅图景指被某个强国牵住的附庸。

senses.title: Going into orbit
senses.definition: used of spacecraft reaching and staying in a path around a body
senses.definitionCN: 指航天器抵达并停留在绕某天体的路径上
senses.example: The rocket put the weather satellite into orbit within an hour.
senses.exampleCN: 火箭在一小时内把气象卫星送入轨道。
senses.why: spaceflight made the phrase everyday, and 'into orbit' became a fixed way to describe a successful launch.
senses.whyCN: 航天让这个短语变得日常，「进入轨道」成了描述发射成功的固定说法。

senses.title: Going round the same subject
senses.titleCN: 比喻：绕着同一个问题打转
senses.definition: figuratively, to keep returning to one topic without settling it
senses.definitionCN: 比喻反复回到同一个话题却始终不解决
senses.example: The meeting orbited the budget question for two hours.
senses.exampleCN: 会议绕着预算问题转了整整两小时。
senses.why: an orbit returns to the same point, so the metaphor describes discussion that moves but never arrives.
senses.whyCN: 轨道会回到同一点，因此这个比喻形容讨论在动却始终不到达。

senses.title: Named orbital regimes
senses.titleCN: 按高度命名的轨道类型
senses.definition: used in fixed names such as low Earth orbit, polar orbit and geostationary orbit
senses.definitionCN: 用于近地轨道、极轨道、地球静止轨道等固定名称
senses.example: Most communication satellites sit in geostationary orbit.
senses.exampleCN: 多数通信卫星位于地球静止轨道。
senses.why: each regime has different uses, so the noun became part of technical labels that say where a satellite works.
senses.whyCN: 各轨道区间用途不同，因此这个名词成为说明卫星工作位置的技术标签的一部分。

intro.en: Orbit comes from Latin orbita 'wheel-rut, track', from orbis 'circle, disk'. English first used it for the eye socket and only later for a heavenly path. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: orbit 来自拉丁 orbita「车辙、轨迹」，其源为 orbis「圆、盘」。英语最早用它指眼窝，后来才指天体路径。年代均为约数。

items.en: Orbita was the rut a wheel leaves, and by extension any beaten track or course.
items.cn: orbita 是车轮留下的辙，引申为任何被踩出的轨迹或行程。

items.en: Orbis meant a circle, a disk or the round world; the track word was built from it.
items.cn: orbis 意为圆、盘或圆形的世界；轨迹一词即由它构成。

items.en: English orbit first named the bony ring around the eye, a sense Latin already had.
items.cn: 英语 orbit 最早指眼周的骨环，这一义拉丁语已有。

items.en: Seventeenth-century astronomy applied the same word to the path of a body, since both are enclosing tracks.
items.cn: 17 世纪天文学把同一个词用于天体路径，因为两者都是围合的轨迹。

items.en: The twentieth century made 'into orbit' a household phrase and added named regimes such as low Earth orbit.
items.cn: 20 世纪使「进入轨道」成为家常用语，并增添了近地轨道等命名区间。

items.en: Source uncertain (deeper origin): the pre-Latin history of orbis is not established, and any older Indo-European form suggested for it is a reconstruction.
items.cn: 来源不确定（更深词源）：orbis 在拉丁语之前的历史没有定论，凡为其提出的更早印欧形式均属重构。

note.en: Group one holds the derived forms that are easily swapped; group two holds words for a route or a turn.
note.cn: 第一组是容易混用的派生形式；第二组是表示路线或一圈的词。

entries.definition: Of an orbit, or in chemistry a noun for an electron's probability region.
entries.definitionCN: 轨道的；化学中也作名词指电子的概率区域。

entries.definition: The present participle, used for something currently in orbit rather than for the path itself.
entries.definitionCN: 现在分词，指当前正在轨运行的事物，而非路径本身。

entries.definition: A spacecraft designed to circle a body; the -er suffix marks the agent, not the path.
entries.definitionCN: 设计用来绕某天体飞行的航天器；-er 后缀标记执行者，而非路径。

entries.definition: A sphere or globe, from the same orbis; it names the round thing, not the track around it.
entries.definitionCN: 球体或圆球，同出 orbis；它命名圆的东西，而非绕它的轨迹。

entries.definition: The path of a moving body, often one that does not repeat; an orbit is the repeating case.
entries.definitionCN: 运动天体的路径，常指不重复者；轨道是其中重复的情形。

entries.definition: A single circling; it names the motion, while orbit names the track.
entries.definitionCN: 绕行一圈；它命名运动，而 orbit 命名轨迹。

entries.definition: A perfectly round curve; orbits are usually ellipses, so circle is only the special case.
entries.definitionCN: 完美的圆形曲线；轨道通常是椭圆，圆只是特例。

entries.definition: The extent something can reach; it overlaps the 'sphere of influence' sense but has no orbital image.
entries.definitionCN: 某物所能达到的范围；与「势力范围」义重叠，但没有轨道意象。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real relations, real compounds and real etymology, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实词族关系、真实搭配与真实词源，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Latin orbita 'wheel-rut': the path is a groove in space.
normal.cn: 拉丁 orbita「车辙」：路径是空间中磨出的沟。

normal.en: English used orbit for the eye socket before it used it for the moon.
normal.cn: 英语先用 orbit 指眼窝，后来才用它指月球。

normal.en: The family runs orbit, orbital, orbiting, orbiter, orbit insertion.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 orbit、orbital、orbiting、orbiter、orbit insertion。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark spaceflight: go into orbit, low Earth orbit, geostationary orbit.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标记航天：进入轨道、近地轨道、地球静止轨道。

normal.en: The electron sense survives in chemistry as the orbital.
normal.cn: 电子义在化学中以 orbital 的形式留存。

abstract.en: Picture a conversation that keeps circling a locked door.
abstract.cn: 想象一场谈话老绕着一扇锁着的门打转。

abstract.en: Picture a small country held in the gravity of a large one.
abstract.cn: 想象一个小国被大国的引力牵住。

abstract.en: Picture a stone skipping around a whirlpool instead of falling in.
abstract.cn: 想象一颗石子绕着旋涡转，而没有掉进去。

examples.en: The moon's orbit is tilted about five degrees from the ecliptic.
examples.cn: 月球轨道相对黄道倾斜约五度。

examples.en: Engineers raised the satellite's orbit to extend its life.
examples.cn: 工程师抬高了卫星轨道以延长其寿命。

examples.en: The discussion orbited the same objection all afternoon.
examples.cn: 整个下午的讨论都绕着同一个反对意见打转。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「哦，比它（orbit）」——哦，它又比它多绕了一圈 → 轨道、绕行

root: 拉丁 orbita「车辙、轨迹」← orbis「圆、盘」；英语先指眼窝，17 世纪起指天体路径。orbis 更深来源不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses run from the track to the act of following it, to one turn, to an electron's cloud, an eye socket, a sphere of influence, a launch, a metaphor and named orbital zones.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项从轨迹出发，到沿轨迹行进、一整圈、电子的云、眼窝、势力范围、一次发射、一个比喻，最后到按高度命名的轨道区间。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a ball on a string, circling a hand and leaving a ring in the air.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只系绳的小球绕手转，在空气里留下一圈痕迹。

branches.en: MOTION AND COUNT: travelling on the path, and one completed lap.
branches.cn: 运动与计数：沿路径行进，以及走完一圈。

branches.en: RINGS AT SMALL SCALE: electron clouds and eye sockets repeat the enclosing circle.
branches.cn: 小尺度的环：电子云与眼窝重复了围合的圆圈。

branches.en: HELD IN PLACE: politics and argument both describe bodies that cannot leave a centre.
branches.cn: 被牵在原处：政治与争论都描述离不开中心的东西。

branches.en: ENGINEERED ORBITS: launches and named regimes turn the path into a destination.
branches.cn: 被工程化的轨道：发射与命名区间把路径变成目的地。

branches.en: ROOT IMAGE: the wheel-rut is the whole family's source.
branches.cn: 根源意象：车辙是整个词族的来源。

intro.en: Orbit is a Latin noun with a small English family built by suffixes for relation, action and agent.
intro.cn: orbit 是一个拉丁名词，英语用表示关系、动作与执行者的后缀构建了一个小词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin orbita 'track' and orbis 'circle' supply orbit and orb; the family has no Greek element.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 orbita「轨迹」与 orbis「圆」提供 orbit 与 orb；这个词族不含希腊成分。

items.example: The Latin word is the direct source of orbit.
items.exampleCN: 这个拉丁词是 orbit 的直接来源。

items.example: Orbis also gives English orb.
items.exampleCN: orbis 也给出英语 orb。

items.example: The satellite reached orbit.
items.exampleCN: 卫星到达轨道。

items.example: The moon orbits the earth.
items.exampleCN: 月球绕地球运行。

items.example: The probe orbited the planet for a year.
items.exampleCN: 探测器绕这颗行星运行了一年。

items.example: An orbiting lab passes overhead.
items.exampleCN: 一座在轨实验室从头顶经过。

items.example: Orbital debris threatens satellites.
items.exampleCN: 轨道碎片威胁卫星。

items.example: The orbiter mapped the surface for years.
items.exampleCN: 轨道飞行器测绘地表多年。
