senses.title: Relating to an orbit
senses.definition: relating to the path of a body around another
senses.definitionCN: 与一个天体绕另一个天体运行的路径有关的
senses.example: The orbital path of the comet was plotted in red.
senses.exampleCN: 彗星的轨道路径用红色绘出。
senses.why: the word is simply orbit plus the adjective suffix -al, so its base sense is 'of the track'.
senses.whyCN: 这个词就是 orbit 加形容词后缀 -al，因此基本义为「轨迹的」。

senses.title: Operating in orbit
senses.definition: used of objects, stations or debris that are actually circling the earth or another body
senses.definitionCN: 指真正绕地球或其他天体运行的物体、设施或碎片
senses.example: A small metal box carries an orbital label showing its path around the earth.
senses.exampleCN: 小金属盒上贴着一张标出它绕地路径的在轨标签。
senses.why: engineers needed a short adjective for 'in orbit', and orbital filled the gap without a phrase like 'in orbit'.
senses.whyCN: 工程师需要一个简短形容词表示「在轨」，orbital 正好填空，不必说「in orbit」。

senses.title: The atomic orbital
senses.definition: a region around a nucleus where an electron is most likely to be found
senses.definitionCN: 原子核周围电子最可能出现的区域
senses.example: Each electron occupies an orbital with a fixed energy.
senses.exampleCN: 每个电子占据一个能量确定的轨道。
senses.why: quantum mechanics replaced circling paths with probability clouds, but kept the old word by turning it into a noun.
senses.whyCN: 量子力学用概率云取代了绕行路径，却把这个旧词转为名词保留下来。

senses.title: The molecular orbital
senses.definition: a spread of electron probability over a whole molecule rather than one atom
senses.definitionCN: 电子概率分布在整个分子而非单个原子上的区域
senses.example: Bonding electrons fill the lowest molecular orbital first.
senses.exampleCN: 成键电子先填满最低的分子轨道。
senses.why: when atoms join, their orbitals combine, so the same noun was extended from atoms to molecules.
senses.whyCN: 原子结合时其轨道也合并，因此同一个名词从原子扩展到了分子。

senses.title: Of the eye socket
senses.definition: relating to the bony cavity around the eye, as in the orbital bone or orbital floor
senses.definitionCN: 与眼周骨腔有关的，如眶骨或眶底
senses.example: The surgeon repaired the orbital floor after the injury.
senses.exampleCN: 受伤后外科医生修复了眶底。
senses.why: Latin used orbita for the socket too, so the adjective carries both the orbit and the eye socket without conflict.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语也用 orbita 指眼窝，因此这个形容词同时承载轨道与眼窝两义而不冲突。

senses.title: Orbital quantities
senses.titleCN: 轨道物理量：速度、周期、平面
senses.definition: used of measurable properties of motion in an orbit, such as velocity, period and plane
senses.definitionCN: 指轨道运动中的可测属性，如速度、周期与平面
senses.example: Orbital velocity falls as the satellite moves farther out.
senses.exampleCN: 卫星越往外，轨道速度越低。
senses.why: once orbits are treated as curves with numbers, the adjective attaches naturally to every quantity describing them.
senses.whyCN: 一旦轨道被当作带数值的曲线，这个形容词自然就附着于描述它们的每个量。

senses.title: An orbital road
senses.definition: in British English, a road that circles a city instead of passing through it
senses.definitionCN: 英式英语中绕城而不穿城的公路
senses.example: Traffic shifted to the orbital motorway within a year.
senses.exampleCN: 不到一年，车流就转到了环城高速上。
senses.why: a ring road does literally go round a centre, so the astronomical picture transferred to traffic planning.
senses.whyCN: 环路确实绕着一个中心走，因此天文学图景被转用到交通规划上。

senses.title: An orbital launch vehicle
senses.titleCN: 具备入轨能力的运载火箭
senses.definition: used of a rocket powerful enough to place a payload into orbit rather than only on a short flight
senses.definitionCN: 指推力足以把载荷送入轨道、而不只是短程飞行的火箭
senses.example: Only an orbital rocket could carry the full laboratory.
senses.exampleCN: 只有具备入轨能力的火箭才能运载整个实验室。
senses.why: the adjective distinguishes reaching space from reaching orbit, a distinction engineers care about.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词区分「到达太空」与「到达轨道」，而工程师很在意这一区别。

intro.en: Orbital is orbit plus the Latin adjective suffix -alis, giving English -al. The noun use for electron clouds dates from twentieth-century quantum chemistry. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: orbital 是 orbit 加拉丁形容词后缀 -alis（英语作 -al）。指电子云的名词用法来自 20 世纪量子化学。年代均为约数。

items.en: Orbita 'wheel-rut, track' is the base, and Latin already used it for the eye socket.
items.cn: orbita「车辙、轨迹」是基础，拉丁语已用它指眼窝。

items.en: Anatomical Latin formed orbitalis 'of the socket', which is the model for the English adjective.
items.cn: 解剖学拉丁语构成 orbitalis「眼窝的」，是英语形容词的模板。

items.en: English borrowed Latin adjectives ending in -alis as -al, so orbit produced orbital.
items.cn: 英语把以 -alis 结尾的拉丁形容词借作 -al，于是 orbit 产生 orbital。

items.en: In the twentieth century the adjective became a noun for an electron's probability region, first for atoms and then for molecules.
items.cn: 20 世纪这个形容词转为名词，指电子的概率区域，先用于原子，再用于分子。

items.en: Space agencies adopted it for anything in orbit: orbital debris, orbital station, orbital launch.
items.cn: 航天机构用它指一切在轨事物：轨道碎片、在轨空间站、入轨发射。

items.en: Source uncertain (first date): the earliest English use of orbital is not firmly dated, and the pre-Latin origin of orbis remains unsettled.
items.cn: 来源不确定（首见年代）：orbital 最早的英语用例没有可靠年代；orbis 在拉丁语之前的来源亦无定论。

note.en: Group one holds the orbit family forms that are often confused; group two holds adjectives of shape and position.
note.cn: 第一组是常被混淆的 orbit 词族形式；第二组是形状与位置类形容词。

entries.definition: The path itself or the act of circling; orbital only describes something related to it.
entries.definitionCN: 路径本身或绕行动作；orbital 只描述与之相关的事物。

entries.definition: A spacecraft that orbits; the -er suffix marks the thing doing the circling.
entries.definitionCN: 绕行的航天器；-er 后缀标记执行绕行的物体。

entries.definition: The participle for the ongoing motion, as in an orbiting telescope.
entries.definitionCN: 表示正在进行的运动的分词，如「在轨望远镜」。

entries.definition: The flat surface an orbit lies in; the two-word phrase names a plane rather than a property.
entries.definitionCN: 轨道所在的平面；这个两词短语命名的是平面，而非属性。

entries.definition: Shaped like a circle; an orbit can be circular, but orbital says nothing about shape.
entries.definitionCN: 圆形的；轨道可以是圆的，但 orbital 不涉及形状。

entries.definition: Turning around a centre; it stresses the motion rather than the path's geometry.
entries.definitionCN: 绕中心转动；强调运动而非路径几何。

entries.definition: Situated on an outer boundary; it resembles the 'orbital road' sense but carries no circle.
entries.definitionCN: 位于外缘的；与「环城路」义相近，但不含圆圈意象。

entries.definition: Relating to space in general; orbital is a much narrower, path-specific adjective.
entries.definitionCN: 泛指与空间有关；orbital 是窄得多、专指路径的形容词。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real suffixes, real compounds and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实后缀、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: orbit + -al: the plain adjective of the track.
normal.cn: orbit + -al：轨迹的普通形容词。

normal.en: Latin orbitalis was first an anatomical word for the eye socket.
normal.cn: 拉丁 orbitalis 最早是解剖学词，指眼窝。

normal.en: The family runs orbit, orbital, orbiter, orbiting, orbitally.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 orbit、orbital、orbiter、orbiting、orbitally。

normal.en: Fixed terms: orbital period, orbital velocity, orbital plane, orbital debris.
normal.cn: 固定术语：轨道周期、轨道速度、轨道平面、轨道碎片。

normal.en: In chemistry the noun orbital names an electron's probability cloud.
normal.cn: 化学中名词 orbital 指电子的概率云。

abstract.en: Picture a ring road drawn around a city that refuses to be crossed.
abstract.cn: 想象一条绕着不肯被穿过的城市画出的环路。

abstract.en: Picture a haze that surrounds a lamp without ever touching it.
abstract.cn: 想象一团雾围着灯，却从不碰到它。

abstract.en: Picture a label on a box that says where the box will forever go.
abstract.cn: 想象盒子上贴着标签，写明它将永远走的路。

examples.en: Orbital debris poses a growing risk to working satellites.
examples.cn: 轨道碎片对工作中的卫星构成越来越大的风险。

examples.en: The orbital period of the station is about ninety minutes.
examples.cn: 该空间站的轨道周期约为九十分钟。

examples.en: Chemists draw the shape of each orbital before predicting a bond.
examples.cn: 化学家在预测成键之前先画出每个轨道的形状。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「哦，比特（orbital）」——哦，它每比特都绕着走 → 轨道的

root: orbit（拉丁 orbita「车辙」）+ 拉丁形容词后缀 -alis（英语 -al）；拉丁 orbitalis 本为解剖学「眼窝的」，20 世纪又转为名词指电子概率区域。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses begin with the plain adjective, then branch to in-orbit hardware, to electron clouds and molecules, to the eye socket, to measured quantities, to a ring road and to a launch vehicle.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从普通形容词开始，再分向在轨硬件、电子云与分子、眼窝、可测物理量、环城公路与运载火箭。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a thin line drawn once around a centre, marking everything that stays near it.
core.cn: 核心意象：绕中心画的一道细线，标记一切靠近它的事物。

branches.en: PROPERTY AND PLACE: the adjective describes a path, then things living on it.
branches.cn: 属性与位置：这个形容词先描述路径，再描述在路径上的事物。

branches.en: QUANTUM REUSE: atoms and molecules keep the old word for a new kind of cloud.
branches.cn: 量子复用：原子与分子用旧词指一种新的云。

branches.en: BODY RING: the eye socket was the word's first English home.
branches.cn: 身体之环：眼窝是这个词最早的英语归宿。

branches.en: ENGINEERING: quantities and launch capability make the orbit a specification.
branches.cn: 工程：物理量与入轨能力把轨道变成一项指标。

branches.en: CITY RING: a road repeats the circle at human scale.
branches.cn: 城市之环：一条路在人的尺度上重复了这个圆。

intro.en: Orbital is a Latin noun plus a Latin adjective suffix; the same suffix turns it into technical terms across several fields.
intro.cn: orbital 是一个拉丁名词加拉丁形容词后缀；同一后缀在多个领域把它变成技术术语。

latinIntro.en: Latin orbita 'track' and orbitalis 'of the socket' supply the base; orbis 'circle' supplies the wider family.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 orbita「轨迹」与 orbitalis「眼窝的」提供基础；orbis「圆」提供更广的词族。

items.example: The orbit is nearly circular.
items.exampleCN: 这条轨道近似圆形。

items.example: The suffix turns orbit into orbital.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把 orbit 变成 orbital。

items.example: Orbital speed depends on height.
items.exampleCN: 轨道速度取决于高度。

items.example: The atom has three filled orbitals.
items.exampleCN: 该原子有三个填满的轨道。

items.meaning: at the level of an orbit
items.example: The two stars are orbitally locked.
items.exampleCN: 这两颗星在轨道上被锁定。

items.example: The orbiter photographed the ice cap.
items.exampleCN: 轨道飞行器拍下了冰盖。

items.example: The two orbits share one orbital plane.
items.exampleCN: 两条轨道共用一个轨道平面。

items.example: Orbital debris can disable a satellite.
items.exampleCN: 轨道碎片能使卫星失效。

definition_zh: 环绕运行的；在轨的；（orbit 的现在分词）绕行
definition_en: moving in a closed path around a body; the present participle of orbit
core_image: 地面站屏幕上一个小点沿闭合曲线一圈圈绕过大洲的轮廓，轨迹拖出一条淡线
scene: 地面站的屏幕上，一颗小点沿着一条闭合曲线一圈圈绕过大洲的轮廓。On the screen, a dot keeps orbiting the outline of a continent.
sceneCN: 这里 orbiting 指「正在绕某天体运行」（第 1 个义项：orbit 的现在分词，表示持续的绕行）；句意为屏幕上一个小点不断绕大陆轮廓运行。图中可辨识物件：地面站屏幕、闭合曲线、移动小点、淡色轨迹、大陆轮廓。

pos.zh: 绕行（orbit 的现在分词）
在轨运行的；环绕的

senses.title: Moving around a body
senses.definition: the present participle of orbit, describing a body that is travelling around another
senses.definitionCN: orbit 的现在分词，描述一个天体正绕另一个天体运行
senses.example: On the screen, a dot keeps orbiting the outline of a continent.
senses.exampleCN: 屏幕上一个小点不断绕大陆轮廓运行。
senses.why: the -ing form marks an action in progress, so orbiting stresses that the circling is happening now rather than that a path exists.
senses.whyCN: -ing 形式标记正在进行的动作，因此 orbiting 强调绕行正在发生，而非路径存在。

senses.title: In-orbit as an attributive
senses.definition: used before a noun for equipment or people working in orbit, as in an orbiting laboratory
senses.definitionCN: 置于名词前，指在轨道上工作的设备或人员，如「在轨实验室」
senses.example: An orbiting telescope avoids most of the atmosphere's blur.
senses.exampleCN: 在轨望远镜避开了大气的大部分模糊效应。
senses.why: English often uses a participle where other languages use a phrase, so 'which is orbiting' compresses into one word.
senses.whyCN: 英语常用分词替代短语，于是「正在轨运行的」被压缩成一个词。

senses.title: A bound body in astronomy
senses.titleCN: 天文学中受束缚的绕行天体
senses.definition: used of a body held by gravity in a closed path rather than passing through once
senses.definitionCN: 指被引力维持在闭合路径上的天体，而非只穿过一次
senses.example: The star has two planets orbiting in opposite directions.
senses.exampleCN: 这颗恒星有两颗行星朝相反方向绕行。
senses.why: a bound orbit repeats, and the participle is the natural way to say that the repetition is still going on.
senses.whyCN: 受束缚的轨道会重复，而现在分词正是表达这种重复仍在继续的自然方式。

senses.title: The old orbiting electron
senses.definition: used in older physics descriptions of electrons circling a nucleus like planets
senses.definitionCN: 用于较早的物理描述，指电子像行星一样绕原子核转
senses.example: Early models spoke of an orbiting electron losing energy as it turned.
senses.exampleCN: 早期模型说绕核电子在转动时损失能量。
senses.why: the planetary picture was taken literally for a time, and the participle preserves that image even though quantum mechanics replaced it.
senses.whyCN: 行星图景一度被照字面使用，即使量子力学取代了它，现在分词仍保留那个意象。

senses.title: Circling a person
senses.definition: figuratively, staying close to a person or group and seeking their attention
senses.definitionCN: 比喻一直靠近某人或某群体并寻求其注意
senses.example: Aides were orbiting the director long before the meeting began.
senses.exampleCN: 会议开始前很久，助手们就围着主管转。
senses.why: the image of satellites around a planet fits social life, where attention acts like gravity.
senses.whyCN: 卫星绕行星的意象契合社交生活，在那里注意力就像引力。

senses.title: The orbiting phase of a mission
senses.definition: used for the part of a space mission after arrival at a body and before landing or return
senses.definitionCN: 指航天任务抵达某天体之后、着陆或返回之前的那一段
senses.example: During the orbiting phase the crew mapped the ice.
senses.exampleCN: 在轨阶段，乘组测绘了冰层。
senses.why: missions are divided into phases, and the participle names the one in which the craft is going round.
senses.whyCN: 任务被划分为若干阶段，而现在分词命名的是航天器正在绕行的那一段。

senses.title: Going round the same point
senses.definition: figuratively, repeatedly returning to an issue without resolving it
senses.definitionCN: 比喻反复回到某个问题却不解决
senses.example: The debate kept orbiting the same unanswered question.
senses.exampleCN: 辩论一直绕着同一个没有答案的问题转。
senses.why: a closed orbit returns, so the participle describes talk that moves but never lands.
senses.whyCN: 闭合轨道会返回，因此现在分词形容谈话在动却从不落地。

senses.title: Rendezvous and docking while in orbit
senses.titleCN: 在轨交会与对接时的状态
senses.definition: used of craft meeting and joining while both are already circling a body
senses.definitionCN: 指两个航天器都已在绕某天体运行的情况下相互接近并对接
senses.example: Two orbiting modules docked without ground control.
senses.exampleCN: 两个在轨舱段在没有地面控制的情况下完成对接。
senses.why: once several objects share an orbit, the participle is the simplest way to say that they are all already circling.
senses.whyCN: 当多个物体共享一条轨道，现在分词是说明它们都已在绕行的最简方式。

intro.en: Orbiting is orbit plus the English participle ending -ing, from Latin orbita 'track'. The word's technical life began with astronomy and continued into spaceflight. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: orbiting 是 orbit 加英语分词词尾 -ing，其源为拉丁 orbita「轨迹」。这个词的技术生命始于天文学，并延续到航天。年代均为约数。

items.en: Orbita meant a wheel-rut or track, and English took it as orbit for a path around a body.
items.cn: orbita 意为车辙或轨迹，英语借作 orbit，指绕天体的路径。

items.en: The old English participle ending -ing turned verbs into ongoing descriptions, so orbit gained orbiting without a new root.
items.cn: 古英语分词词尾 -ing 把动词变成进行中的描述，因此 orbit 无需新词根就得到 orbiting。

items.en: Writers used the participle for bodies in bound motion: a planet orbiting its star.
items.cn: 作者们用这个分词指处于束缚运动的天体：绕其恒星运行的行星。

items.en: Nineteenth- and early twentieth-century physics spoke of orbiting electrons before quantum mechanics changed the picture.
items.cn: 19 世纪与 20 世纪初的物理学在量子力学改变图景之前，谈的是绕核电子。

items.en: Space agencies made the participle routine in phrases such as orbiting laboratory and orbiting phase.
items.cn: 航天机构让这个分词在「在轨实验室」「在轨阶段」等短语中成为常规用法。

items.en: Source uncertain (first date): the earliest attributive use of orbiting is not firmly dated, and the pre-Latin origin of orbis remains unsettled.
items.cn: 来源不确定（首见年代）：orbiting 最早的定语用法没有可靠年代；orbis 在拉丁语之前的来源亦无定论。

note.en: Group one holds the orbit family forms that differ only by ending; group two holds verbs of turning.
note.cn: 第一组是只靠词尾区分的 orbit 词族形式；第二组是表示转动的动词。

entries.definition: The noun or the plain verb; orbiting is only the same verb caught in the middle of happening.
entries.definitionCN: 名词或动词原形；orbiting 只是同一个动词被截取在发生之中。

entries.definition: A relational adjective meaning 'of an orbit'; it does not say that motion is happening now.
entries.definitionCN: 表示「轨道的」关系形容词；它不表示运动正在发生。

entries.definition: A noun for the spacecraft itself, not for its motion.
entries.definitionCN: 指航天器本身的名词，而非其运动。

entries.definition: The finished action, used when the circling is over or viewed as a whole.
entries.definitionCN: 已完成的动作，用于绕行结束或整体看待时。

entries.definition: Going round in a circle, with no claim about gravity or a star; the plain counterpart of orbiting.
entries.definitionCN: 绕圈走，不涉及引力或恒星；是 orbiting 的日常对应词。

entries.definition: Turning around a centre, often used of wheels or platforms rather than celestial bodies.
entries.definitionCN: 绕中心转动，常用于轮子或平台而非天体。

entries.definition: Turning about an internal axis, as a planet does daily; orbiting is going round something else.
entries.definitionCN: 绕自身轴转动，如行星每日自转；orbiting 是绕别的物体。

entries.definition: Forming a ring around something, often without motion, as a wall encircles a town.
entries.definitionCN: 在周围围成一圈，常不含运动，如城墙围住城镇。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real endings, real compounds and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实词尾、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: orbit + -ing: the action of circling, caught in progress.
normal.cn: orbit + -ing：绕行动作，被截取在进行中。

normal.en: The family runs orbit, orbits, orbited, orbiting, orbital, orbiter.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 orbit、orbits、orbited、orbiting、orbital、orbiter。

normal.en: Fixed phrases: orbiting satellite, orbiting laboratory, orbiting telescope.
normal.cn: 固定搭配：在轨卫星、在轨实验室、在轨望远镜。

normal.en: The participle suits mission phases: the orbiting phase comes before landing.
normal.cn: 这个分词适合任务阶段：在轨阶段在着陆之前。

normal.en: Old physics said orbiting electron before quantum clouds replaced the picture.
normal.cn: 旧物理说「绕核电子」，后来量子云取代了这幅图。

abstract.en: Picture a moth that cannot leave a lamp but never touches it.
abstract.cn: 想象一只飞蛾离不开灯，却从不碰到它。

abstract.en: Picture a conversation that goes round a locked door all evening.
abstract.cn: 想象一场谈话整晚绕着一扇锁着的门。

abstract.en: Picture two trains on parallel rings, meeting at the same point each hour.
abstract.cn: 想象两列车在平行的环上，每小时在同一点相遇。

examples.en: An orbiting satellite can read a ship's position within metres.
examples.cn: 一颗在轨卫星能把船只位置读到米级。

examples.en: The crew spent four days orbiting the planet before descent.
examples.cn: 乘组在下降前绕这颗行星飞了四天。

examples.en: Two orbiting observatories crossed the same patch of sky.
examples.cn: 两个在轨天文台扫过同一片天空。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「哦，比特 ing」——哦，它每一比特都在绕着走 → 环绕运行的

root: orbit（拉丁 orbita「车辙」）+ 古英语分词词尾 -ing；表示正在进行的绕行。天体义始于天文学，航天用语沿用至今。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses take one ending through its uses: the ongoing action, the attributive 'in orbit', astronomy's bound body, the old electron, a person others circle, a mission phase, a debate going round and two craft docking.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项带着同一个词尾走过各种用途：正在进行的动作、定语的「在轨」、天文学的束缚天体、旧的电子图景、被人围绕的人、任务阶段、绕圈子的辩论，以及两器对接。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a small dot drawing a closed curve, and the curve still being drawn.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个小点画出闭合曲线，而曲线仍在被画出。

branches.en: THE EPITHET: as a modifier it names work done while circling.
branches.cn: 作定语：它修饰在环绕中完成的工作。

branches.en: TWO PICTURES OF CIRCLING: astronomy's bound body and physics' old electron.
branches.cn: 两种绕行图景：天文学的束缚天体与物理学的旧电子。

branches.en: ATTENTION AND ARGUMENT: people and debates both keep something at their centre.
branches.cn: 注意力与争论：人和辩论都把某物留在中心。

branches.en: OPERATIONS: a phase of a mission and a meeting of two orbiting craft.
branches.cn: 运行：任务的一个阶段，以及两个在轨航天器的相遇。

branches.en: GRAMMAR AT THE ROOT: the ending is why the word means 'happening now'.
branches.cn: 语法即根源：词尾正是这个词意为「正在发生」的原因。

intro.en: Orbiting is a Latin-derived noun turned into an English participle; the ending carries the 'in progress' meaning.
intro.cn: orbiting 是拉丁来源的名词变成英语分词；词尾承载「正在进行」的意思。

latinIntro.en: The base orbit comes from Latin orbita 'track' and orbis 'circle'; the -ing ending is native English, not Latin.
latinIntro.cn: 词基 orbit 来自拉丁 orbita「轨迹」与 orbis「圆」；-ing 词尾是英语本族成分，并非拉丁语。

items.example: The orbit is stable.
items.exampleCN: 这条轨道是稳定的。

items.example: The ending makes orbit into orbiting.
items.exampleCN: 这个词尾把 orbit 变成 orbiting。

items.example: A dot keeps orbiting the outline.
items.exampleCN: 一个小点不断绕轮廓运行。

items.example: The moon orbits the earth.
items.exampleCN: 月球绕地球运行。

items.example: The craft orbited for six days.
items.exampleCN: 航天器绕行了六天。

items.example: Orbital data was relayed to the ground.
items.exampleCN: 轨道数据被传回地面。

items.example: The orbiter released a lander.
items.exampleCN: 轨道飞行器释放了一个着陆器。

items.example: The orbiting laboratory hosted six crew.
items.exampleCN: 这座在轨实验室接待了六名乘员。

definition_zh: 卫星（天然或人造）；附属机构；卫星城；卫星国；随从
definition_en: a body that orbits a larger one, especially a moon, or a human-made craft placed in orbit
core_image: 屋顶的碟形天线对准夜空，一个亮点匀速划过星幕，天线随它缓缓转动
scene: 夜里屋顶的天线旁，一颗亮点匀速划过星空，碟面正对着它缓缓转动。A dish on the roof turns toward a satellite moving steadily across the sky.
sceneCN: 这里 satellite 指「人造卫星」（第 2 个义项：被送入轨道运行的人造航天器）；句意为屋顶碟形天线转向一颗匀速划过天空的卫星。图中可辨识物件：碟形天线、夜空、移动亮点、支架、屋脊。

pos.zh: 卫星；人造卫星；附属机构；卫星城；卫星国；随从

senses.title: A natural moon
senses.definition: a natural body that orbits a planet or smaller body
senses.definitionCN: 绕行星或更小天体运行的天然天体
senses.example: Jupiter has more than ninety known natural satellites.
senses.exampleCN: 木星已知的天然卫星超过九十颗。
senses.why: the word first meant an attendant, and a moon was seen as a body that accompanies its planet.
senses.whyCN: 这个词最初意为随从，而卫星被视为陪伴行星的天体。

senses.title: A human-made craft in orbit
senses.definition: an object built and launched to orbit the earth or another body for a purpose
senses.definitionCN: 为某种用途建造并送入绕地球或其他天体轨道的人造物体
senses.example: A dish on the roof turns toward a satellite moving steadily across the sky.
senses.exampleCN: 屋顶的碟形天线转向一颗匀速划过天空的卫星。
senses.why: once people could launch their own attendants, the old word transferred from moons to machines without any change of shape.
senses.whyCN: 当人们能发射自己的「随从」后，这个旧词从月球转到机器上，形状一点没变。

senses.title: A satellite town or campus
senses.definition: a smaller settlement or branch that depends on a larger centre nearby
senses.definitionCN: 依赖附近更大中心的小型聚落或分支
senses.example: The university built a satellite campus across the river.
senses.exampleCN: 这所大学在河对岸建了一个分校。
senses.why: a dependent place circles a main centre economically the way a moon circles a planet.
senses.whyCN: 依附的地方在经济上绕着主中心转，正如卫星绕行星转。

senses.title: A satellite state
senses.definition: a country formally independent but controlled by a stronger power
senses.definitionCN: 名义上独立却受更强国家控制的国度
senses.example: The treaty left the smaller neighbour a satellite state in all but name.
senses.exampleCN: 该条约使这个较小邻国除名义外成了卫星国。
senses.why: politics reused the astronomical picture because such a state is held in another's orbit rather than free.
senses.whyCN: 政治沿用天文学图景，因为这样的国家被留在别人的轨道上，而非自由。

senses.title: Kinds of working satellites
senses.definition: used of purpose-built satellites such as communications, weather, navigation and reconnaissance craft
senses.definitionCN: 指按用途建造的卫星，如通信、气象、导航与侦察卫星
senses.example: Weather satellites gave the coast two days of warning.
senses.exampleCN: 气象卫星给海岸带来了两天的预警。
senses.why: each purpose gives the noun a modifier, so 'satellite' becomes a category name rather than one object.
senses.whyCN: 每种用途都给这个名词加一个修饰语，于是 satellite 成了类别名而非单个物体。

senses.title: Named orbital regimes
senses.definition: used with orbit names such as geostationary, polar and low Earth orbit
senses.definitionCN: 与地球静止、极地、近地等轨道名称连用
senses.example: A geostationary satellite stays above one point on the equator.
senses.exampleCN: 地球静止卫星停在赤道某一点的上空。
senses.why: the same craft can serve different purposes depending on where it circles, so the orbit name attaches to the noun.
senses.whyCN: 同一颗卫星因绕行位置不同而用途不同，因此轨道名称附着在这个名词上。

senses.title: Satellite television and signals
senses.definition: used attributively for services and equipment that relay signals through an orbiting craft
senses.definitionCN: 作定语指通过在轨航天器中继信号的服务与设备
senses.example: Satellite television reached villages with no cable.
senses.exampleCN: 卫星电视到达了没有电缆的村庄。
senses.why: everyday use shortens 'by satellite' into a noun modifier, so the word now appears before dishes, feeds and channels.
senses.whyCN: 日常用法把「经由卫星」缩成名词修饰语，于是这个词出现在天线、信号与频道之前。

senses.title: An attendant or follower
senses.definition: historically, a person who attends or escorts another, often with a hint of dependence
senses.definitionCN: 历史上指陪侍或护送他人的人，常带依附意味
senses.example: In the old court, a satellite was a noble's armed companion.
senses.exampleCN: 在旧时宫廷里，satellite 是贵族的武装随从。
senses.why: this is the word's oldest sense, and every later use keeps its shape: something that moves with something larger.
senses.whyCN: 这是这个词最古老的义项，后来每个用法都保留同一形状：某物伴随更大的某物移动。

senses.title: Satellite DNA
senses.definition: in genetics, short repeated DNA sequences that sit apart from the main repeats
senses.definitionCN: 遗传学中与主要重复序列分开的短重复 DNA 片段
senses.example: Satellite DNA varies greatly between individuals.
senses.exampleCN: 卫星 DNA 在个体之间差异很大。
senses.why: the fragments were named for sitting beside the main band, like small companions beside a large body.
senses.whyCN: 这些片段因位于主带旁边而得名，像大天体旁的小伴星。

intro.en: Satellite comes from Latin satelles, satellitis 'attendant, guard', a word whose deeper origin is uncertain. It became an astronomical term in the seventeenth century and a space term after 1957. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: satellite 来自拉丁 satelles、satellitis「随从、护卫」，其更深来源不确定。它在 17 世纪成为天文学术语，1957 年后又成为航天术语。年代均为约数。

items.en: Satelles meant a bodyguard or attendant who moves with a more powerful person; its origin is debated and possibly not Latin at all.
items.cn: satelles 指随更强之人行动的护卫或随从；其来源有争议，可能根本不是拉丁语固有词。

items.en: English took satellite in the sixteenth century for a follower or hanger-on, often with contempt.
items.cn: 英语在 16 世纪借入 satellite，指随从或攀附者，常带轻蔑。

items.en: Kepler applied the Latin word to the moons of Jupiter, and the astronomical sense spread quickly.
items.cn: 开普勒把这个拉丁词用于木星的卫星，天文学义迅速传播。

items.en: Twentieth-century politics borrowed it for dependent countries, extending the 'attendant' image to states.
items.cn: 20 世纪政治借它指依附国家，把「随从」意象扩展到国家。

items.en: After 1957 the word usually meant a human-made craft, and everyday compounds such as satellite dish followed.
items.cn: 1957 年后，这个词通常指人造航天器，随之出现 satellite dish 等日常复合词。

items.en: Source uncertain (deeper origin): satelles has no agreed etymology, and suggestions linking it to Etruscan or to a Latin root are hypotheses rather than demonstrated derivations.
items.cn: 来源不确定（更深词源）：satelles 没有公认的词源，把它联系到伊特鲁里亚语或某个拉丁词根的种种说法都只是假说，并非已证实的派生。

note.en: Group one holds near neighbours in space; group two holds words for something dependent on a larger centre.
note.cn: 第一组是太空中的邻近概念；第二组是表示依附于更大中心的事物。

entries.definition: The everyday word for a natural satellite, especially the earth's; satellite is the technical and wider term.
entries.definitionCN: 天然卫星（尤指地球的）日常词；satellite 是更技术、更宽的说法。

entries.definition: An uncrewed craft sent to explore; it may orbit, fly by or land, so it is not always a satellite.
entries.definitionCN: 派去探测的无人航天器；它可绕行、飞掠或着陆，因此不总是卫星。

entries.definition: A craft designed specifically to circle a body; it is a kind of satellite but not every satellite is an orbiter.
entries.definitionCN: 专门设计绕某天体飞行的航天器；它是卫星的一种，但并非每颗卫星都是轨道器。

entries.definition: The dish that sends and receives signals; it is named for the satellite but stays on the ground.
entries.definitionCN: 收发信号的碟形天线；因卫星得名，却留在地面。

entries.definition: A territory controlled by another state; it matches the 'satellite state' sense without the orbital image.
entries.definitionCN: 受另一国控制的地区；对应「卫星国」义，但不含轨道意象。

entries.definition: A small settlement or office far from the main base; close to 'satellite campus' but without dependence.
entries.definitionCN: 远离主基地的小据点或办事处；接近「分校」义，但不含依附。

entries.definition: A person who follows another; it matches the oldest sense of satellite but has no astronomy.
entries.definitionCN: 跟随他人的人；对应 satellite 最古老的义项，但与天文学无关。

entries.definition: A person who serves or escorts; the closest everyday equivalent of the Latin source.
entries.definitionCN: 服务或陪同的人；是最接近拉丁源义的日常词。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real compounds, real history and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实搭配、真实历史与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Latin satelles 'attendant': a satellite is a body that attends a bigger one.
normal.cn: 拉丁 satelles「随从」：卫星就是陪伴更大天体的天体。

normal.en: The same word covers moons, machines, branch campuses and client states.
normal.cn: 同一个词覆盖月球、机器、分校与附庸国。

normal.en: Fixed compounds: communications satellite, weather satellite, satellite dish.
normal.cn: 固定搭配：通信卫星、气象卫星、卫星天线。

normal.en: Orbit names attach to it: geostationary satellite, polar satellite, low Earth orbit satellite.
normal.cn: 轨道名称附在它上面：地球静止卫星、极轨卫星、近地轨道卫星。

normal.en: Genetics has satellite DNA, named for sitting beside the main band.
normal.cn: 遗传学有卫星 DNA，因位于主带旁边而得名。

abstract.en: Picture a small boat tied to a larger one, moving wherever it moves.
abstract.cn: 想象一条小船系在大船上，大船去哪它去哪。

abstract.en: Picture a lamp on a hill that lights a valley it does not belong to.
abstract.cn: 想象山丘上一盏灯，照亮一个它并不属于的山谷。

abstract.en: Picture a town that has its own mayor but no independent budget.
abstract.cn: 想象一个有自己镇长却没有独立预算的镇。

examples.en: The satellite sends images every ninety minutes.
examples.cn: 这颗卫星每九十分钟传回一次图像。

examples.en: Mars has two small natural satellites, Phobos and Deimos.
examples.cn: 火星有两颗小天然卫星：火卫一与火卫二。

examples.en: The old capital became a satellite of the new industrial city.
examples.cn: 这座旧都成了新兴工业城市的卫星城。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「撒特莱特（satellite）」——撒出去、特立独行地绕着他转 → 卫星

root: 拉丁 satelles、satellitis「随从、护卫」，更深来源不确定（有伊特鲁里亚语假说）；17 世纪经开普勒用于木星卫星，1957 年后主要指人造航天器。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses begin with the moon, move to the machine and to dependent places and states, then to purpose and orbit types, to relay services, back to the attendant and finally to a genetic fragment.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项从月球开始，转向人造机器、依附的场所与国家，再到用途与轨道类型、中继服务，最后回到随从与一段基因片段。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a small light moving steadily around a larger body, attended by a dish below.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个小亮点稳定地绕更大天体移动，地面有碟形天线相随。

branches.en: ATTEND: the oldest sense and the moon share one gesture of accompanying.
branches.cn: 随行：最古老的义项与月球共享同一个陪伴动作。

branches.en: MACHINES BY PURPOSE: craft, their jobs and their orbits.
branches.cn: 按用途分的机器：航天器、任务与轨道。

branches.en: DEPENDENT PLACES: a campus and a country both circle a stronger centre.
branches.cn: 依附之地：分校与国家都绕更强的中心转。

branches.en: SIGNAL PATH: television and data travel through the craft.
branches.cn: 信号路径：电视与数据经由航天器传输。

branches.en: SMALL BESIDE LARGE: a DNA fragment repeats the same spatial picture.
branches.cn: 大旁之小：一段 DNA 重复了同一空间图景。

intro.en: Satellite is a single Latin noun with no split into prefix and root; its English family is mostly compounds rather than suffixes.
intro.cn: satellite 是一个不可再分的拉丁名词，无前缀与词根之分；它的英语词族多为复合词而非后缀派生。

latinIntro.en: Latin satelles supplies the whole word; Kepler's Latin coinage satellitium helped fix the astronomical sense.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 satelles 提供整个词；开普勒所造的拉丁词 satellitium 帮助固定了天文学义。

items.example: The Latin noun is the whole source of the English word.
items.exampleCN: 这个拉丁名词就是英语词的全部来源。

items.meaning: a body or craft in orbit
items.example: The satellite crossed the sky.
items.exampleCN: 卫星划过天空。

items.example: Two satellites share the same orbit.
items.exampleCN: 两颗卫星共享同一条轨道。

items.meaning: a ground antenna for satellite signals
items.meaningCN: 接收卫星信号的地面天线
items.example: The satellite dish points south.
items.exampleCN: 卫星天线朝南。

items.example: The satellite state had little say in policy.
items.exampleCN: 这个卫星国在政策上几乎没有发言权。

items.example: The satellite town grew around the railway.
items.exampleCN: 卫星城沿着铁路发展起来。

items.example: Satellite imagery showed the flood's edge.
items.exampleCN: 卫星影像显示了洪水的边缘。

items.example: Satellite television arrived before the road.
items.exampleCN: 卫星电视比公路先到。

latinEntries.structure: satellitium, satellitii (n., second declension; modern Latin coinage)
latinEntries.meaning: a group of attendant bodies, used for moons
latinEntries.meaningCN: 一群随行天体，用于指卫星

definition_zh: 天然卫星；自然形成、绕行星运行的天体（与人造卫星相对）
definition_en: a naturally formed body that orbits a planet or a smaller solar-system body
core_image: 讲解牌前，一颗灰白小球绕着大球转，旁边的小牌写明它未经任何发射
scene: 展厅的讲解牌上，一颗灰白小球绕着一颗大球运行，旁边注明它并非任何人造装置。The label explains that a natural satellite formed without any human launch.
sceneCN: 这里 natural satellite 指「自然形成、绕行星运行的天体」（第 1 个义项：与人造卫星相对）；句意为牌子说明天然卫星未经任何人类发射而形成。图中可辨识物件：讲解牌、灰白小球、大球、绕行箭头、展台灯。

pos.zh: 天然卫星（可数，复数指多颗）

collocations.zh: 天然卫星与人造卫星之别

senses.title: A moon, not a machine
senses.titleCN: 天然形成的卫星，而非机器
senses.definition: a body that formed by natural processes and orbits a planet or smaller body
senses.definitionCN: 由自然过程形成、绕行星或更小天体运行的天体
senses.example: The label explains that a natural satellite formed without any human launch.
senses.exampleCN: 牌子说明天然卫星未经任何人类发射而形成。
senses.why: the phrase exists mainly to draw a line: after 1957 'satellite' could mean a machine, so 'natural' had to be added.
senses.whyCN: 这个短语主要用来划界：1957 年后 satellite 可指机器，因此必须加上 natural。

senses.title: The moons of the solar system
senses.titleCN: 太阳系各行星的卫星群
senses.definition: collectively, the hundreds of moons counted around the planets and dwarf planets
senses.definitionCN: 合计指各行星与矮行星周围数以百计的卫星
senses.example: The solar system's natural satellites number in the hundreds.
senses.exampleCN: 太阳系的天然卫星数以百计。
senses.why: once telescopes and probes found moons everywhere, the phrase became the collective label for all of them.
senses.whyCN: 当望远镜与探测器在各处发现卫星后，这个短语成了它们的集合标签。

senses.title: Tidal locking
senses.definition: the state in which a natural satellite keeps one face toward its planet
senses.definitionCN: 天然卫星始终以同一面朝向其行星的状态
senses.example: Most large natural satellites are tidally locked to their planets.
senses.exampleCN: 多数大型天然卫星都被潮汐锁定在各自的行星上。
senses.why: close moons are slowed by their planet's tides until spin and orbit match, a fact the phrase often carries.
senses.whyCN: 近距卫星被行星潮汐拖慢，直到自转与公转同步，这个短语常承载这一事实。

senses.title: How they form
senses.definition: used of the processes that produce moons: accretion in a disk, impact debris or gravitational capture
senses.definitionCN: 指产生卫星的过程：盘中吸积、撞击碎片或引力俘获
senses.example: Capture is one route by which a natural satellite joins a planet.
senses.exampleCN: 俘获是天然卫星加入某行星的一条途径。
senses.why: formation is the main way astronomers classify moons, so the phrase often appears beside models of origin.
senses.whyCN: 形成方式是天文学家给卫星分类的主要依据，因此这个短语常与起源模型同现。

senses.title: Regular and irregular moons
senses.titleCN: 规则卫星与不规则卫星
senses.definition: used in the classification by orbit: regular moons go the planet's way in near-circular paths, irregular ones do not
senses.definitionCN: 按轨道分类：规则卫星顺行星自转方向近圆运行，不规则卫星则不然
senses.example: The planet's irregular natural satellites travel far out and backwards.
senses.exampleCN: 该行星的不规则天然卫星在远处逆行。
senses.why: orbit shape records origin, so the phrase pairs naturally with the regular and irregular labels.
senses.whyCN: 轨道形状记录着起源，因此这个短语自然与规则、不规则两类标签搭配。

senses.title: Worlds with oceans and volcanoes
senses.titleCN: 有海洋与火山的卫星世界
senses.definition: used of large moons studied as worlds in their own right, with ice, atmospheres or volcanism
senses.definitionCN: 指被当作独立世界研究的大型卫星，有冰、大气或火山活动
senses.example: One natural satellite of Jupiter may hold a deep ocean under its ice.
senses.exampleCN: 木星的一颗天然卫星可能在冰下拥有深海。
senses.why: the phrase marks that these bodies are not mere points but places with geology worth studying.
senses.whyCN: 这个短语标明这些天体不只是光点，而是有值得研究的地质的地方。

senses.title: Naming rules
senses.definition: used in the context of the official naming of moons by the international astronomical body
senses.definitionCN: 用于国际天文机构对卫星的正式命名语境
senses.example: A newly found natural satellite waits years for an official name.
senses.exampleCN: 新发现的天然卫星要等上数年才获正式名字。
senses.why: because such bodies are numerous and faint, an official register is needed, and the phrase appears in those rules.
senses.whyCN: 这类天体数量多且暗淡，需要一份正式名录，而这个短语就出现在这些规则里。

senses.title: Watching one from earth
senses.definition: used of amateur or telescopic observation of a moon's brightness, phase or motion
senses.definitionCN: 指业余或望远镜观测卫星的亮度、相位与运动
senses.example: A small telescope can follow the natural satellite's nightly motion.
senses.exampleCN: 一台小望远镜就能追踪这颗天然卫星每夜的运动。
senses.why: before spacecraft, everything known about moons came from watching their motion, so the phrase belongs to observation as well as to theory.
senses.whyCN: 在航天器之前，关于卫星的一切都来自观测其运动，因此这个短语既属理论也属观测。

intro.en: Natural satellite joins natural, from Latin natura 'nature', to satellite, from Latin satelles 'attendant'. The phrase became standard when artificial satellites made the distinction necessary. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: natural satellite 由 natural（源自拉丁 natura「本性」）与 satellite（源自拉丁 satelles「随从」）组合。当人造卫星使区分成为必要，这个短语才成为标准。年代均为约数。

items.en: Natura meant birth, character and the order of things, from nasci 'to be born'; naturalis 'of nature' came from it.
items.cn: natura 意为出生、本性、万物秩序，来自 nasci「出生」；naturalis「自然的」由此而来。

items.en: Satelles meant an attendant or guard; its deeper origin is uncertain and possibly not Latin.
items.cn: satelles 意为随从或护卫；其更深来源不确定，可能并非拉丁语固有。

items.en: From the seventeenth century satellite named a moon, and natural was added when precision was needed.
items.cn: 从 17 世纪起 satellite 指卫星，需要精确时会加上 natural。

items.en: Artificial satellites made the contrast unavoidable, and 'natural satellite' became the standard technical phrase.
items.cn: 人造卫星使这一对照不可避免，natural satellite 成为标准技术短语。

items.en: Modern planetary science uses the phrase for every moon, from lumpy small bodies to Titan-sized worlds.
items.cn: 现代行星科学用这个短语指所有卫星，从形状不规则的小天体到土卫六大小的世界。

items.en: Source uncertain (first date and deeper origin): the first use of the exact phrase is not firmly dated, and the etymology of satelles remains unsettled.
items.cn: 来源不确定（首见年代与更深词源）：这一确切短语的最早用例没有可靠年代；satelles 的词源亦无定论。

note.en: Group one holds the terms that differ only by origin; group two holds words for a small companion body.
note.cn: 第一组是只因来源不同而区分的术语；第二组是表示小伴体的词。

entries.definition: The general word for anything orbiting a larger body, natural or built.
entries.definitionCN: 泛指绕更大天体运行之物，天然的或人造的。

entries.definition: A human-made craft in orbit; it is defined by contrast with the natural kind.
entries.definitionCN: 在轨的人造航天器；其定义正与天然一类相对。

entries.definition: The common word for a natural satellite, especially the earth's; it is shorter and less technical.
entries.definitionCN: 天然卫星的日常词，尤指地球的；更短、更不技术化。

entries.definition: The body a moon orbits; the two words mark the two ends of one relationship.
entries.definitionCN: 卫星所绕的天体；两词标记同一关系的两端。

entries.definition: A very small moon, often a temporary ring particle; the -let suffix marks small size.
entries.definitionCN: 极小的卫星，常为暂时的环中颗粒；-let 后缀标记小。

entries.definition: A neutral term for a smaller body travelling with a larger one, used when the class is unclear.
entries.definitionCN: 指随较大天体运行之较小天体的中性说法，用于类别不明时。

entries.definition: A body that orbits the primary in a pair; it says nothing about how it formed.
entries.definitionCN: 双天体系统中绕主天体运行者；不涉及形成方式。

entries.definition: Broken pieces in orbit, natural or artificial; it is not a coherent satellite.
entries.definitionCN: 在轨的碎块，天然或人造；并非成形的卫星。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real compounds, real terms and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实搭配、真实术语与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: natural 'formed by nature' + satellite 'attendant': a moon that formed on its own.
normal.cn: natural「自然形成的」+ satellite「随从」：自行形成的卫星。

normal.en: The phrase became standard after 1957 to separate moons from machines.
normal.cn: 1957 年后这个短语成为标准，用来把月球与机器分开。

normal.en: Most large moons are tidally locked, showing one face to their planet.
normal.cn: 多数大型卫星被潮汐锁定，只以一面朝向行星。

normal.en: Regular moons follow the planet's spin; irregular ones are captured and often retrograde.
normal.cn: 规则卫星顺着行星自转；不规则卫星多为被俘获且常逆行。

normal.en: The family runs satellite, moon, moonlet, artificial satellite, lunar.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 satellite、moon、moonlet、artificial satellite、lunar。

abstract.en: Picture a pebble that has been going round a boulder since before any map existed.
abstract.cn: 想象一颗小石子，在有地图之前就绕着巨石转。

abstract.en: Picture a dancer always facing the same partner, never showing her back.
abstract.cn: 想象一个舞者始终面向同一搭档，从不转身。

abstract.en: Picture a child born in a house and never once leaving the yard.
abstract.cn: 想象一个生在这屋里、从未离开院子的孩子。

examples.en: Earth's natural satellite is unusually large for its planet.
examples.cn: 地球的天然卫星相对其行星大得异常。

examples.en: New natural satellites are still being found around Saturn.
examples.cn: 土星周围仍在发现新的天然卫星。

examples.en: A natural satellite can be captured from a passing asteroid.
examples.cn: 天然卫星可能由路过的小行星被俘获而成。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「自然的（natural）＋ 撒特莱特（satellite）」——自己长出来、绕着转的伴星 → 天然卫星

root: natural 源自拉丁 natura「本性」（nasci「出生」）+ -alis；satellite 源自拉丁 satelles「随从」，更深来源不确定；短语在 1957 年后与人造卫星对举而固定。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses define the term by contrast with machines, then apply it to the solar system's moons, to locking, formation, orbit classes, living worlds, naming and observation.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项先用与人造物的对照定义术语，再用于太阳系卫星群、潮汐锁定、形成方式、轨道类别、有活动世界的卫星、命名规范与观测。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a grey ball circling a larger one, with no launch tower anywhere.
core.cn: 核心意象：一颗灰球绕着更大的球，周围没有任何发射塔。

branches.en: THE CENSUS: the phrase counts every moon that qualifies.
branches.cn: 清点：这个短语清点所有合格的卫星。

branches.en: PHYSICS OF ARRIVAL: locking and formation explain how a moon settles into place.
branches.cn: 到来的物理：锁定与形成解释了卫星如何安顿下来。

branches.en: CLASSES AND WORLDS: orbit shape sorts them, and some become places in their own right.
branches.cn: 类别与世界：轨道形状给它们分类，有些则成为独立的地方。

branches.en: NAMING AND SEEING: official registers and small telescopes both handle these faint bodies.
branches.cn: 命名与看见：正式名录与小望远镜都在对付这些暗淡天体。

branches.en: THE CONTRAST: 'natural' is the whole point of the phrase.
branches.cn: 对照：「natural」正是这个短语的全部要点。

intro.en: The phrase is two Latin-derived words: an adjective from natura and a noun from satelles, with no prefix involved.
intro.cn: 这个短语由两个拉丁来源的词构成：一个来自 natura 的形容词，一个来自 satelles 的名词，不涉及前缀。

latinIntro.en: Latin natura and naturalis supply the first word, satelles the second; the compound phrase itself is modern English.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 natura 与 naturalis 提供第一个词，satelles 提供第二个；短语本身是近代英语。

items.example: The root also gives natural and native.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根还给出 natural 与 native。

items.example: Naturalis became English natural.
items.exampleCN: naturalis 成为英语 natural。

items.example: The word is behind satellite.
items.exampleCN: satellite 即出自这个词。

items.example: A natural arch spans the cove.
items.exampleCN: 一座天然拱桥横跨小湾。

items.example: The satellite is faint but regular.
items.exampleCN: 这颗卫星暗淡但有规律。

items.example: The label names a natural satellite.
items.exampleCN: 牌子上写的是一颗天然卫星。

items.example: Artificial satellites outnumber the visible moons.
items.exampleCN: 人造卫星数量超过可见卫星。

items.example: A moonlet may survive only a few years.
items.exampleCN: 一颗小卫星可能只存在几年。

definition_zh: 月亮；月球；卫星；（诗）月光；（动词）闲荡、出神；（英俚）露出臀部
definition_en: the natural body that orbits the earth, or any natural satellite of a planet
core_image: 院墙上方一轮圆月升到屋脊那么高，瓦片被照出淡蓝色的光
scene: 院墙上方，一轮圆月升到屋脊那么高，瓦片被照出淡蓝的光。Above the courtyard wall, the moon has risen level with the roof tiles.
sceneCN: 这里 moon 指「绕地球运行的天然卫星，即月球」（第 1 个义项：地球的天然卫星）；句意为院墙上方，月亮已升到与屋瓦齐高。图中可辨识物件：院墙、圆月、屋脊、瓦片、淡蓝月色。

pos.zh: 月球；月亮；卫星；月光
闲荡、出神；（英俚）露出臀部

senses.title: The earth's natural satellite
senses.definition: the body that orbits the earth and causes tides and eclipses
senses.definitionCN: 绕地球运行、引起潮汐与食象的天体
senses.example: Above the courtyard wall, the moon has risen level with the roof tiles.
senses.exampleCN: 院墙上方，月亮已升到与屋瓦齐高。
senses.why: the word is native English, not borrowed, because the moon is the one sky object everyone could name without astronomy.
senses.whyCN: 这个词是英语本族词而非借词，因为月亮是无需天文学人人都会命名的天体。

senses.title: Its visible shape and phases
senses.definition: the moon as seen from earth, changing shape through the month
senses.definitionCN: 从地球所见的月亮，其形状在一个月里变化
senses.example: A thin crescent moon hung just above the hills.
senses.exampleCN: 一弯细细的月牙挂在山丘上方。
senses.why: what people call 'the moon' is usually the lit part they can see, so the word names an appearance as well as a body.
senses.whyCN: 人们所说的「月亮」通常指能看见的那部分亮面，因此这个词既指天体也指外观。

senses.title: Any planet's moon
senses.definition: a natural satellite of any planet, not only the earth's
senses.definitionCN: 任何行星的天然卫星，不限于地球的
senses.example: Jupiter's moons were the first found beyond our own.
senses.exampleCN: 木星的卫星是最早在我们月球之外被发现的。
senses.why: once Galileo saw four points circling Jupiter, the common noun extended from one moon to many.
senses.whyCN: 当伽利略看到四个光点绕木星后，这个普通名词便从一个月亮扩展到许多个。

senses.title: Moonlight
senses.definition: the light reflected from the moon, especially in literary use
senses.definitionCN: 月球反射的光，尤用于文学语言
senses.example: They walked home by the light of the moon.
senses.exampleCN: 他们借着月光走回家。
senses.why: since the moon's light is its most noticeable effect on earth, the noun easily stands for the light itself.
senses.whyCN: 月之光是对地球最显著的影响，因此这个名词很容易代指光本身。

senses.title: Many moons ago
senses.definition: in the fixed phrase many moons ago, meaning a long time in the past
senses.definitionCN: 固定短语「许多个月亮以前」，意为很久以前
senses.example: Many moons ago this field was an orchard.
senses.exampleCN: 很久以前，这片地是一座果园。
senses.why: a moon also meant a month, so counting moons was counting months, and the phrase keeps that older reckoning.
senses.whyCN: moon 也曾指一个月，因此数月亮就是数月份，这个短语保留了这种古老算法。

senses.title: To moon about
senses.definition: to spend time aimlessly or dreamily, as in mooning around the house
senses.definitionCN: 无所事事或恍恍惚惚地消磨时间，如在家里闲荡
senses.example: He mooned about the garden all afternoon.
senses.exampleCN: 他整个下午都在花园里闲荡。
senses.why: the verb pictures someone drifting like a moon across the sky, with no fixed direction.
senses.whyCN: 这个动词把人想成像月亮一样在天上漂移，没有固定方向。

senses.title: British slang: to moon
senses.definition: in informal British use, to show one's bare buttocks as a joke or insult
senses.definitionCN: 英式口语中，为玩笑或羞辱而露出光屁股
senses.example: The comedian mooned the crowd and was booed.
senses.exampleCN: 那个喜剧演员对观众露臀，被喝了倒彩。
senses.why: the slang sense plays on a pale round shape, but it is a separate development and should not be confused with the astronomy.
senses.whyCN: 这个俚语义借的是苍白圆形的样子，但它是独立发展出来的，不应与天文学义混淆。

senses.title: A lunar month
senses.definition: the period of the moon's cycle, about twenty-nine and a half days, once used to measure months
senses.definitionCN: 月亮盈亏一周的时长，约二十九天半，曾用来计量月份
senses.example: The festival follows the moon rather than the sun.
senses.exampleCN: 这个节日按月亮而非太阳计算。
senses.why: month and moon come from the same root, so the calendar still carries the moon's cycle inside it.
senses.whyCN: month 与 moon 同出一根，因此历法里仍装着月亮的周期。

senses.title: Promise the moon
senses.definition: in idioms such as promise the moon, to offer something impossible
senses.definitionCN: 在「许诺月亮」等习语中，指许下不可能兑现的事
senses.example: Politicians promise the moon and deliver a lamp.
senses.exampleCN: 政客许诺月亮，却只送来一盏灯。
senses.why: the moon is visibly out of reach, which makes it the natural object for a promise no one can keep.
senses.whyCN: 月亮显然够不着，因此它自然成了无人能兑现的承诺的对象。

intro.en: Moon is native English, from Old English mōna, from Proto-Germanic *mēnô and a reconstructed Indo-European stem for 'moon, month'. It is not related to Latin luna. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: moon 是英语本族词，来自古英语 mōna、原始日耳曼语 *mēnô，再往前是表示「月亮、月份」的印欧词干重构形式。它与拉丁 luna 没有直接关系。年代均为约数。

items.en: Old English mōna named the moon and also stood for a month, a link still visible in month and Monday.
items.cn: 古英语 mōna 指月亮，也指一个月；这一联系仍见于 month 与 Monday。

items.en: The Proto-Germanic form *mēnô is reconstructed from the Germanic languages; no written record of it survives.
items.cn: 原始日耳曼语形式 *mēnô 由各日耳曼语言重构而来，没有书面记录留存。

items.en: The stem usually written *mḗh₁n̥s meant both 'moon' and 'month' and is a reconstruction, not an attested word.
items.cn: 通常写作 *mḗh₁n̥s 的词干兼指「月亮」与「月份」，属重构形式，并非有记录的词。

items.en: The same root idea connects the moon to measuring time, which is why month, Monday and 'many moons' all belong here.
items.cn: 同一词根把月亮与计时联系起来，因此 month、Monday 与「many moons」都属此处。

items.en: Latin luna 'moon' comes from a different root connected with light, and gives lunar, not moon.
items.cn: 拉丁 luna「月亮」来自另一个与光有关的词根，派生的是 lunar，而非 moon。

items.en: Source uncertain (deeper origin): the exact Indo-European shape and its relation to the 'measure' root are debated, so the form given here is a reconstruction.
items.cn: 来源不确定（更深词源）：确切的印欧形态及其与「测量」词根的关系仍有争议，此处给出的形式属重构。

note.en: Group one holds words built on the same native stem; group two holds sky words that overlap in use.
note.cn: 第一组是同出本族词干的词；第二组是用法重叠的天空词。

entries.definition: A unit of the calendar, from the same root as moon; it names time, not the body.
entries.definitionCN: 历法单位，与 moon 同根；命名时间，而非天体。

entries.definition: Literally 'moon's day', a calque of Latin dies lunae; it keeps the older religious naming.
entries.definitionCN: 字面「月亮之日」，仿译拉丁 dies lunae；保留了更古老的宗教命名。

entries.definition: The light reflected by the moon; a compound, not a second object.
entries.definitionCN: 月球反射的光；是复合词，不指第二个天体。

entries.definition: A very small natural satellite; the -let suffix marks size, not kind.
entries.definitionCN: 极小的天然卫星；-let 后缀标记大小，而非种类。

entries.definition: The general word for any orbiting body, natural or artificial; moon is the everyday and native word.
entries.definitionCN: 泛指任何绕行天体，天然或人造；moon 是日常的本族词。

entries.definition: The curved shape of a waxing or waning moon; it names a phase, not the body.
entries.definitionCN: 盈缺月牙的弯曲形状；命名月相，而非天体。

entries.definition: The Latin-derived adjective for the moon; it replaces 'of the moon' in technical writing.
entries.definitionCN: 源自拉丁的月球形容词；在技术文字中替代「月亮的」。

entries.definition: An old word for a heavenly light, especially sun or moon; it treats the moon as a lamp.
entries.definitionCN: 指天空发光体的旧词，尤指日月；把月亮当作一盏灯。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real relatives, real compounds and real idioms, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实同族词、真实搭配与真实习语，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: moon and month share one root: a moon was a way of counting time.
normal.cn: moon 与 month 同根：月亮曾是计时方式。

normal.en: Monday is literally the moon's day.
normal.cn: Monday 字面就是「月亮之日」。

normal.en: The family runs moon, moons, moonlight, moonlit, moonlet, lunar.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 moon、moons、moonlight、moonlit、moonlet、lunar。

normal.en: Phases are fixed phrases: full moon, new moon, crescent moon, moon phase.
normal.cn: 月相是固定搭配：满月、新月、月牙、月相。

normal.en: Two idioms mark the word: many moons ago, once in a blue moon.
normal.cn: 两个习语标记这个词：很久以前、千载难逢。

abstract.en: Picture a lamp that changes its shape every night but never moves its post.
abstract.cn: 想象一盏灯每晚换形状，却从不挪动位置。

abstract.en: Picture a coin that is sometimes a thin edge and sometimes a full face.
abstract.cn: 想象一枚硬币，有时只见薄边，有时见整面。

abstract.en: Picture a promise written on something nobody can reach.
abstract.cn: 想象把承诺写在一个谁也够不着的东西上。

examples.en: The moon rises about fifty minutes later each night.
examples.cn: 月亮每晚大约晚五十分钟升起。

examples.en: Saturn has more moons than any other planet.
examples.cn: 土星的卫星比任何其他行星都多。

examples.en: They met once in a blue moon, usually by the river.
examples.cn: 他们难得见一面，通常在河边。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「木嗯（moon）」——夜里抬头「嗯」一声看见的那轮圆盘 → 月亮

root: 古英语 mōna ← 原始日耳曼语 *mēnô ← 印欧词干 *mḗh₁n̥s（兼指月亮与月份，属重构形式）；与拉丁 luna 不同源，luna 另出与光有关的词根。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses keep one object but change the angle: the body, its visible phase, other planets' moons, its light, its use as a month, two verbs, a calendar cycle and an impossible promise.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项守着同一个天体，却不断换角度：天体、可见月相、别行星的卫星、它的光、它当月份、两个动词义、历法周期，以及一个够不着的承诺。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a round pale light above a wall, changing shape but staying in the sky.
core.cn: 核心意象：墙上方一轮淡色圆光，形状会变，却始终在天上。

branches.en: OBJECT AND LOOK: the same word names the body and the shape people see.
branches.cn: 天体与外观：同一个词既指天体，也指人们看见的形状。

branches.en: FROM ONE TO MANY: Galileo's four points made moon a countable class.
branches.cn: 从一到多：伽利略看到的四个光点使 moon 成为可数类别。

branches.en: LIGHT AND TIME: the moon gives light and once gave the month.
branches.cn: 光与时间：月亮给光，也曾给月份。

branches.en: IDIOMATIC REACH: counting moons measures the past, and promising one measures impossibility.
branches.cn: 习语中的尺度：数月亮量过去，许月亮量不可能。

branches.en: VERBAL DRIFT: drifting like a moon, and a slang joke on its pale round shape.
branches.cn: 动词漂移：像月亮一样漂，以及拿它苍白圆形开的俚语玩笑。

intro.en: Moon is a single native English root; its family is built by compounding and by the small suffix -let, not by Latin prefixes.
intro.cn: moon 是单一的英语本族词根；其词族靠复合与小型后缀 -let 构成，不用拉丁前缀。

latinIntro.en: Latin used luna for the moon, a different root; English technical adjectives come from it, while the noun itself stays native.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语用 luna 指月亮，属另一词根；英语技术形容词由它而来，而名词本身仍是本族词。

items.example: The moon rose over the wall.
items.exampleCN: 月亮升到墙上方。

items.example: The probe visited several moons.
items.exampleCN: 探测器造访了数颗卫星。

items.example: Moonlight lay across the floor.
items.exampleCN: 月光铺在地板上。

items.example: They crossed the moonlit field.
items.exampleCN: 他们穿过月光下的田野。

items.example: A moonlet orbits inside the ring.
items.exampleCN: 一颗小卫星在环内运行。

items.example: The moon landing was watched worldwide.
items.exampleCN: 登月被全世界观看。

items.example: The month follows the moon's cycle.
items.exampleCN: 月份随月亮周期而定。

items.example: Monday is named for the moon.
items.exampleCN: Monday 因月亮而得名。

latinEntries.meaning: the day of the moon, Monday

scene: 桌上摊开一本旧历，纸页边角画着月牙，红笔圈出按月亮排定的节气。The old calendar on the desk marks its dates by a lunar cycle.
sceneCN: 这里 lunar 指「按月亮周期计算的」（第 3 个义项：阴历的、按月的）；句意为桌上那本旧历按月亮周期排定日期。图中可辨识物件：旧历、月牙图案、红笔圈记、桌面、窗光。

senses.title: Of the moon
senses.definition: relating to the moon as a body, its position or its motion
senses.definitionCN: 指作为天体的月球、其位置或运动
senses.example: Lunar gravity is about one sixth of the earth's.
senses.exampleCN: 月球引力约为地球的六分之一。
senses.why: the adjective comes straight from the Latin noun for the moon, so it simply attaches 'moon' to another noun.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词直接来自拉丁语「月亮」名词，因此只是把「月亮」挂到另一个名词上。

senses.title: Of the moon's surface
senses.definition: used of the surface, soil, rocks and missions that reach the moon
senses.definitionCN: 指月球表面、月壤、月岩与抵达月球的探测活动
senses.example: The lunar dust clung to the astronauts' boots.
senses.exampleCN: 月尘粘在宇航员的靴子上。
senses.why: once spacecraft could land, the adjective shifted from the sky to the ground underfoot.
senses.whyCN: 当航天器能够着陆后，这个形容词便从天空转到了脚下的地面。

senses.title: Calculated by the moon
senses.definition: used of calendars and dates fixed by the moon's cycle rather than the sun's
senses.definitionCN: 指按月亮周期而非太阳周期确定的历法与日期
senses.example: The old calendar on the desk marks its dates by a lunar cycle.
senses.exampleCN: 桌上那本旧历按月亮周期排定日期。
senses.why: a month was once counted by moons, so calendars that keep that reckoning are called lunar rather than solar.
senses.whyCN: 一个月曾按月亮计数，因此沿用这种算法的历法被称为 lunar，而非 solar。

senses.title: Phases and cycles
senses.definition: used of the moon's changing lit shape and the cycle it repeats
senses.definitionCN: 指月亮亮面形状的变化及其重复的周期
senses.example: Lunar phases repeat roughly every twenty-nine and a half days.
senses.exampleCN: 月相大约每二十九天半重复一次。
senses.why: the cycle is the moon's most regular behaviour, so the adjective often names time measured by that repetition.
senses.whyCN: 这一周期是月亮最规律的行为，因此这个形容词常命名按该重复计量的时间。

senses.title: The moon's pull on the sea
senses.definition: used of tides produced mainly by the moon's gravity
senses.definitionCN: 指主要由月球引力产生的潮汐
senses.example: The lunar tide is stronger than the sun's contribution.
senses.exampleCN: 月潮比太阳的贡献更强。
senses.why: the moon pulls the ocean more strongly than the distant sun, so tides are labelled by which body drives them.
senses.whyCN: 月球对海洋的牵引比遥远的太阳更强，因此潮汐按驱动它的天体来标记。

senses.title: Lunar orbit and bases
senses.definition: used of spacecraft paths around the moon and plans for structures on it
senses.definitionCN: 指绕月球的航天器路径以及在其上建造设施的规划
senses.example: The capsule entered lunar orbit on the third day.
senses.exampleCN: 太空舱在第三天进入月球轨道。
senses.why: space agencies needed to distinguish orbits at the moon from those at the earth, so 'lunar' became a routine prefix.
senses.whyCN: 航天机构需要区分月球轨道与地球轨道，于是 lunar 成了常用的前置限定词。

senses.title: Lunar deities and astrology
senses.definition: used of a god identified with the moon, or of astrological charts built on lunar positions
senses.definitionCN: 指与月亮等同的神，或依据月亮位置排出的星盘
senses.example: Roman writers described a lunar goddess with a crescent crown.
senses.exampleCN: 罗马作家描写过一位戴月牙冠的月亮女神。
senses.why: worship and astrology treat the moon as a power with a personality, keeping the adjective's oldest, personal use.
senses.whyCN: 崇拜与占星把月亮当作有人格的力量，保留了这个形容词最古老、人格化的用法。

senses.title: Lunar caustic
senses.titleCN: 旧医学术语：硝酸银（月牙剂）
senses.definition: in an old medical term, lunar caustic, silver nitrate used to burn away tissue
senses.definitionCN: 旧医学名词「月牙剂」，指用来烧灼组织的硝酸银
senses.example: Surgeons once used lunar caustic to close small wounds.
senses.exampleCN: 外科医生曾用月牙剂来处理小伤口。
senses.why: alchemists marked silver with the moon's sign, so a silver compound carried 'lunar' into medicine.
senses.whyCN: 炼金术士用月亮符号标记银，于是含银的化合物把这个词带进了医学。

intro.en: Lunar comes from Latin lunaris 'of the moon', from luna 'moon'. Luna's own origin is often connected with a root meaning 'light', but that link is reconstructed. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: lunar 来自拉丁 lunaris「月亮的」，源头是 luna「月亮」。luna 自身的来源常被联系到一个意为「光」的词根，但这一联系属重构。年代均为约数。

items.en: Luna was both the moon and the moon goddess; like sol for the sun, one word served both roles.
items.cn: luna 既是月亮，也是月亮女神；如同 sol 之于太阳，一个词兼两职。

items.en: Many accounts derive luna from an older form meaning 'the shining one', related to lux 'light'; this is a reconstruction, not a recorded word.
items.cn: 许多说法把 luna 追溯到意为「发光者」的更早形式，与 lux「光」相关；这是重构，并非有记录的词。

items.en: The adjective lunaris 'of the moon' was formed with -alis, the suffix English later took as -al.
items.cn: 形容词 lunaris「月亮的」由 -alis 构成，英语后来把这个后缀借作 -al。

items.en: English borrowed lunar in the late Middle Ages, mostly in astronomy and medicine.
items.cn: 英语在中世纪末期借入 lunar，多用于天文学与医学。

items.en: English keeps native moon for the everyday object and Latin lunar for technical relations, a typical doublet.
items.cn: 英语用本族词 moon 指日常对象，用拉丁词 lunar 指技术关系，这是典型的同义双层词。

items.en: Source uncertain (deeper origin): the link between luna and the 'light' root is plausible but unproven, and any older Indo-European form for it is a reconstruction.
items.cn: 来源不确定（更深词源）：luna 与「光」词根的联系虽合理却未获证明，凡为其给出的更早印欧形式均属重构。

note.en: Group one holds Latin-derived words from the same luna stem; group two holds words describing moonlight and night.
note.cn: 第一组是同出 luna 词干的拉丁来源词；第二组是描述月光与夜晚的词。

entries.definition: The interval between two new moons; it turns the adjective's root into a measure of time.
entries.definitionCN: 两次新月之间的间隔；把词根变成时间量度。

entries.definition: Historically 'moon-struck', from the old belief that phases affected the mind; it is not a neutral medical word today.
entries.definitionCN: 历史上意为「被月亮击中的」，源于月相影响心智的旧信念；今天不是中性的医学词。

entries.definition: The pale half-moon at the base of a nail; a diminutive of luna, naming a shape.
entries.definitionCN: 指甲根部淡色半月；是 luna 的指小形式，命名一种形状。

entries.definition: Situated beneath the moon, hence earthly and changeable in old cosmology.
entries.definitionCN: 位于月亮之下，故在旧宇宙论中指尘世且可变的。

entries.definition: Reached by moonlight, as a moonlit path; it describes a result, not a relation.
entries.definitionCN: 被月光照到的，如月光下的小路；描述结果而非关系。

entries.definition: Active or occurring at night; lunar concerns the moon, not the whole night.
entries.definitionCN: 夜间活动或发生的；lunar 关乎月亮，而非整个夜晚。

entries.definition: Belonging to the sky in general; lunar is one narrow part of the celestial.
entries.definitionCN: 泛指属于天空；lunar 只是其中很窄的一部分。

entries.definition: The curved sickle shape of a young or old moon; it names a form rather than a relation.
entries.definitionCN: 新月或残月的弯曲镰形；命名形状而非关系。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real suffixes, real terms and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实后缀、真实术语与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Latin luna 'moon' + -aris: the technical adjective of the moon.
normal.cn: 拉丁 luna「月亮」+ -aris：月亮的技术形容词。

normal.en: English keeps both: moon for the object, lunar for the relation.
normal.cn: 英语两词并用：moon 指对象，lunar 指关系。

normal.en: Fixed terms: lunar surface, lunar landing, lunar calendar, lunar module.
normal.cn: 固定术语：月面、登月、阴历、登月舱。

normal.en: The family runs lunation, lunatic, lunula, sublunary.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 lunation、lunatic、lunula、sublunary。

normal.en: Alchemists marked silver with the moon, hence lunar caustic.
normal.cn: 炼金术士用月亮标记银，故有「月牙剂」之说。

abstract.en: Picture a calendar whose pages are cut in the shape of a crescent.
abstract.cn: 想象一本日历，纸页都剪成月牙形。

abstract.en: Picture a sea that rises because something far above is pulling it.
abstract.cn: 想象一片海因为高处某物牵引而上涨。

abstract.en: Picture a silver coin stamped with a small moon.
abstract.cn: 想象一枚银币上压印着一轮小月亮。

examples.en: The lunar surface is covered with fine grey dust.
examples.cn: 月面覆盖着细灰的尘埃。

examples.en: The lunar calendar keeps the months aligned with the moon.
examples.cn: 阴历让月份与月亮保持一致。

examples.en: A lunar eclipse happens when the earth's shadow covers the moon.
examples.cn: 当地球的影子遮住月亮时，就发生月食。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「露娜（luna）」——月光女神露娜 → 月球的

root: 拉丁 luna「月亮」+ 形容词后缀 -alis（英语 -ar）→ lunaris → lunar。luna 与意为「光」的词根联系属重构，未获证明。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses move from the body to its surface, to the calendar it once set, to its phases, its tide, its orbits, its gods and finally a silver compound.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从天体走到它的表面、它曾定下的历法、它的月相、它的潮汐、它的轨道、它的神祇，最后落到一种银化合物。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a crescent printed in the corner of an old calendar page.
core.cn: 核心意象：旧日历纸角上印着的一弯月牙。

branches.en: BODY AND GROUND: from the object in the sky to the dust underfoot.
branches.cn: 天体与地面：从天上对象到脚下尘土。

branches.en: TIME BY THE MOON: calendars and phases both count its cycle.
branches.cn: 按月计时：历法与月相都在数它的周期。

branches.en: PULL: the moon's gravity becomes a tide with its name.
branches.cn: 牵引：月球引力变成以它命名的潮。

branches.en: PATHS AND GODS: engineering orbits and old worship share the adjective.
branches.cn: 路径与神祇：工程轨道与古老崇拜共用这个形容词。

branches.en: ALCHEMY: silver was the moon's metal, so medicine kept the word.
branches.cn: 炼金术：银是月亮的金属，因此医学保留了这个词。

intro.en: Lunar is a Latin noun plus a Latin adjective suffix; the root also forms several words through diminutive and prefix changes.
intro.cn: lunar 是拉丁名词加拉丁形容词后缀；同一词根还通过指小与前置成分构成若干词。

latinIntro.en: Latin luna and lunaris supply the core; lux 'light' is the root often proposed behind luna, though the link is reconstructed.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 luna 与 lunaris 提供核心；lux「光」是常被认为在 luna 背后的词根，但这一联系属重构。

items.example: The root also gives lunation and lunula.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根还给出 lunation 与 lunula。

items.example: Lunaris became English lunar.
items.exampleCN: lunaris 成为英语 lunar。

items.example: Lunar dust is sharp and dry.
items.exampleCN: 月尘锋利而干燥。

items.example: A lunation lasts about twenty-nine days.
items.exampleCN: 一个朔望月约二十九天。

items.meaningCN: 被月亮影响的；精神失常的
items.example: The word records an old belief about phases.
items.exampleCN: 这个词记录了一种关于月相的旧信念。

items.example: The lunula sits at the nail's base.
items.exampleCN: 指甲半月位于指甲根部。

items.example: Old cosmology divided the sublunary from the eternal.
items.exampleCN: 旧宇宙论把月下世界与永恒世界分开。

items.example: The lunar module had thin walls.
items.exampleCN: 登月舱的壁很薄。

definition_zh: 日食；月食；（天体）掩食；使黯然失色；失势、声望衰退
definition_en: the hiding of one heavenly body by another, especially the sun by the moon or the moon by the earth's shadow
core_image: 操场上人们举着带滤光片的纸板，太阳被黑影咬出一个缺口，天色像傍晚
scene: 操场上一群人举着带滤光片的纸板，太阳被月影咬出一个缺口，光线变得像傍晚。Through the filter, the sun shows a growing eclipse.
sceneCN: 这里 eclipse 指「一个天体遮住另一个天体的现象，此处为日食」（第 1 个义项：日食）；句意为透过滤光片看，太阳正被吞出一个逐渐扩大的缺口。图中可辨识物件：滤光纸板、太阳缺口、操场人群、偏暗天色、影子。

pos.zh: 食象；日食；月食；掩食；失势
遮住（光）；使黯然失色；压倒

derivatives.zh: 正在遮住的；掩盖他者的
黄道；黄道的（同根，不同义）

senses.title: A solar eclipse
senses.definition: the event in which the moon passes between the earth and the sun and hides part or all of the sun
senses.definitionCN: 月球运行到地球与太阳之间，遮住太阳一部分或全部的事件
senses.example: Through the filter, the sun shows a growing eclipse.
senses.exampleCN: 透过滤光片看，太阳正被吞出一个逐渐扩大的缺口。
senses.why: Greek ekleipsis meant 'a failing to appear', and a darkened sun is exactly a light that has failed to show.
senses.whyCN: 希腊 ekleipsis 意为「未能出现」，而变暗的太阳正是一盏未能显现的灯。

senses.title: A lunar eclipse
senses.definition: the event in which the earth's shadow falls across the moon
senses.definitionCN: 地球的影子落在月球上的事件
senses.example: The moon turned copper during the lunar eclipse.
senses.exampleCN: 月食期间月亮变成了铜红色。
senses.why: the same word covers both directions because in each case one body hides another's light.
senses.whyCN: 同一个词覆盖两个方向，因为两种情形都是一个天体挡住另一个的光。

senses.title: Any occultation
senses.definition: in astronomy, any event in which one body passes in front of another and hides it
senses.definitionCN: 天文学中一个天体从另一个前面经过并遮住它的事件
senses.example: A star's eclipse by a planet revealed the planet's atmosphere.
senses.exampleCN: 行星掩住一颗恒星，从而揭示了它自己的大气。
senses.why: astronomers extended the word beyond sun and moon to any such alignment, since the geometry is identical.
senses.whyCN: 天文学家把这个词从日月扩展到任何此类连线，因为几何关系完全相同。

senses.title: To block light
senses.definition: to cut off light from something, as one body does to another
senses.definitionCN: 挡住照向某物的光，如一个天体对另一个天体所做
senses.example: The larger moon eclipses the smaller one every few days.
senses.exampleCN: 较大的卫星每隔几天就遮住较小的那颗。
senses.why: the noun became a verb by the ordinary English route, naming the act that produces the event.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词按英语常规路径转为动词，命名产生该事件的动作。

senses.title: To surpass and overshadow
senses.definition: figuratively, to be so much better or larger that another thing stops being noticed
senses.definitionCN: 比喻某事物好得多或大得多，使另一事物不再被注意
senses.example: Her second novel eclipsed everything she had written before.
senses.exampleCN: 她的第二部小说盖过了她此前写的一切。
senses.why: a total eclipse leaves no light from the hidden body, so the metaphor is about being outshone rather than defeated.
senses.whyCN: 全食时被遮住的天体不留一点光，因此这个比喻说的是被比下去，而非被打败。

senses.title: In eclipse, out of favour
senses.definition: in the phrase in eclipse, having lost prominence or favour for a time
senses.definitionCN: 用于短语「处于失势」，指一时失去显要地位或宠爱
senses.example: The theory spent twenty years in eclipse before returning.
senses.exampleCN: 这个理论失势二十年之后又回来了。
senses.why: when a body is eclipsed it is temporarily invisible, so the phrase describes fame that has gone dark for a while.
senses.whyCN: 天体被食时暂时不可见，因此这个短语形容名声暂时暗了下去。

senses.title: Total, partial and annular
senses.definition: used in fixed labels for how much of the sun or moon is covered and in what geometry
senses.definitionCN: 用于固定标签，说明日月被遮住多少以及何种几何关系
senses.example: An annular eclipse leaves a ring of sunlight visible.
senses.exampleCN: 环食会留下一圈可见的阳光。
senses.why: the labels exist because distance and alignment decide whether the covering is complete or leaves a ring.
senses.whyCN: 这些标签存在，是因为距离与连线决定遮盖是完整的还是留下一圈。

senses.title: The eclipse cycle
senses.definition: the repeating rhythm, roughly eighteen years, on which similar eclipses recur and can be predicted
senses.definitionCN: 相似食象重复出现并可被预报的节律，约十八年
senses.example: Ancient astronomers used the cycle to predict the next eclipse.
senses.exampleCN: 古代天文学家利用这个周期预报下一次食。
senses.why: because the rhythm is regular, the word also names the timetable, not only the event.
senses.whyCN: 由于节律规律，这个词也命名时刻表，而不只是事件本身。

senses.title: The eclipse phase in virology
senses.definition: in virology, the period after a virus enters a cell when no complete virus can be detected
senses.definitionCN: 病毒进入细胞后、检测不到完整病毒的那段时间
senses.example: During the eclipse phase the virus seems to vanish.
senses.exampleCN: 在隐蔽期，病毒似乎消失了。
senses.why: the virus is present but invisible to assay, exactly the state the astronomical word describes.
senses.whyCN: 病毒仍在，却检测不到，正是这个天文学词所描述的状态。

intro.en: Eclipse comes from Greek ekleipsis 'abandonment, failure to appear', from ekleipein 'to leave out, fail'. It reached English through Latin and French. The figurative sense is early modern. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: eclipse 来自希腊 ekleipsis「抛弃、未能出现」，源自动词 ekleipein「遗漏、失败」。它经拉丁语与法语进入英语。比喻义出现于近代早期。年代均为约数。

items.en: Ekleipsis meant a leaving out or a failure, especially of a heavenly body to appear as expected.
items.cn: ekleipsis 意为遗漏或失败，尤指天体未如预期出现。

items.en: The verb combined ek- 'out' with leipein 'to leave', giving 'to leave out, forsake, fail'.
items.cn: 这个动词由 ek-「出」与 leipein「离开」组合，意为「遗漏、抛弃、失败」。

items.en: Greek leipein and Latin linquere 'to leave' descend from the same Indo-European root, so relic and eclipse are distant cousins.
items.cn: 希腊 leipein 与拉丁 linquere「离开」同出印欧词根，因此 relic 与 eclipse 是远亲。

items.en: Latin borrowed the Greek noun as eclipsis, and medieval writers used it for both sun and moon.
items.cn: 拉丁语借作 eclipsis，中世纪作者用它指日食与月食。

items.en: English eclipse appears in the Middle Ages; the sense 'to outshine' develops later and is common by the seventeenth century.
items.cn: 英语 eclipse 见于中世纪；「使黯然失色」义后来发展，到 17 世纪已常见。

items.en: Source uncertain (first date): the earliest English use is not firmly dated, and the precise Indo-European shape behind leipein is a reconstruction.
items.cn: 来源不确定（首见年代）：最早的英语用例没有可靠年代；leipein 背后确切的印欧形态属重构。

note.en: Group one holds words from the same Greek root with different meanings; group two holds terms for one body hiding another.
note.cn: 第一组是同出希腊词根但意义不同的词；第二组是一个天体遮住另一个的术语。

entries.definition: The plane of the sun's apparent yearly path, named from the same root because eclipses occur on it; it is a path, not an event.
entries.definitionCN: 太阳视运动年路径所在的平面，因食发生于此而得名；它是路径，而非事件。

entries.definition: From Greek elleipsis 'a falling short', with en- 'in' rather than ek- 'out'; it means words left out, not light hidden.
entries.definitionCN: 来自希腊 elleipsis「欠缺」，用 en-「在内」而非 ek-「在外」；指省略的词，而非被遮的光。

entries.definition: The closed oval from the same 'falling short' root; orbits are ellipses, but an ellipse is not an eclipse.
entries.definitionCN: 同出「欠缺」词根的闭合椭圆；轨道是椭圆，但椭圆不是食。

entries.definition: The roughly eighteen-year cycle after which similar eclipses recur; it names the rhythm rather than the darkening.
entries.definitionCN: 约十八年的周期，相似食象此后重现；命名节律，而非变暗本身。

entries.definition: The passing of one body in front of another, from Latin 'hiding'; it is the technical term where eclipse is the familiar one.
entries.definitionCN: 一个天体从另一个前面经过，来自拉丁「隐藏」；是 eclipse 的技术对应词。

entries.definition: The passage of a small body across the face of a larger one; the small body is seen, so it is not always an eclipse.
entries.definitionCN: 小天体横过大天体表面；小天体可见，因此不总是食。

entries.definition: To cast a shadow over or surpass; it matches the 'outshine' sense without astronomy.
entries.definitionCN: 投下阴影或超过；对应「使黯然失色」义，但不涉天文学。

entries.definition: To keep something from being seen, usually on purpose; an eclipse hides light by geometry, not intention.
entries.definitionCN: 有意不让人看见；食是按几何关系遮光，而非有意。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real roots, real terms and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实词根、真实术语与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Greek ek- 'out' + leipein 'leave': the light leaves, so the body fails to appear.
normal.cn: 希腊 ek-「出」+ leipein「离开」：光离开了，于是天体未能出现。

normal.en: Latin linquere 'to leave' shares the root, which links eclipse to relic.
normal.cn: 拉丁 linquere「离开」共享词根，把 eclipse 与 relic 联系起来。

normal.en: Fixed terms: solar eclipse, lunar eclipse, total, partial, annular.
normal.cn: 固定术语：日食、月食、全食、偏食、环食。

normal.en: The family runs eclipses, eclipsed, eclipsing, eclipse phase, ecliptic.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 eclipses、eclipsed、eclipsing、eclipse phase、ecliptic。

normal.en: The saros cycle of about eighteen years lets astronomers predict eclipses.
normal.cn: 约十八年的沙罗周期让天文学家能预报食。

abstract.en: Picture a hand passing in front of a lamp and taking the room's light with it.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手从灯前经过，把屋里的光也带走。

abstract.en: Picture a famous singer walking on stage and making the opening act invisible.
abstract.cn: 想象一位名歌手登台，让暖场者变得无人看见。

abstract.en: Picture a virus that is there but cannot be found for a while.
abstract.cn: 想象一种病毒明明在场，却有一阵子找不到。

examples.en: Never look at a solar eclipse without a proper filter.
examples.cn: 绝不要在没有合适滤光片的情况下直视日食。

examples.en: The new bridge eclipsed every earlier attempt to cross the river.
examples.cn: 这座新桥盖过了此前所有跨河尝试。

examples.en: The comet spent a decade in eclipse before observers returned to it.
examples.cn: 这颗彗星失势十年后，观测者才重新关注它。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「一个 lips（嘴唇）」——一个嘴唇把太阳含住 → 日食

root: 希腊 ekleipsis「未能出现」← ekleipein「遗漏、离开」＝ ek-「出」+ leipein「离开」，与拉丁 linquere「离开」同根；经拉丁 eclipsis、法语进入英语。leipein 的印欧形态属重构。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses begin with the darkened sun, move to the darkened moon, to any occultation, to the verb of blocking, to outshining, to lost favour, to the labels of totality, to the cycle and finally to a virus that cannot be found.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项从变暗的太阳开始，走到变暗的月亮、任何掩食、遮光的动词、盖过他人、失势、全食偏食等标签、周期，最后落到一种找不到的病毒。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a dark bite taken out of a bright disk, with the sky turning dusk.
core.cn: 核心意象：明亮圆盘被咬出一个黑色缺口，天色转暗。

branches.en: TWO DIRECTIONS: the moon hides the sun, then the earth's shadow hides the moon.
branches.cn: 两个方向：月球遮太阳，地球影子遮月球。

branches.en: GEOMETRY AND LABELS: any alignment counts, and distance decides total, partial or annular.
branches.cn: 几何与标签：任何连线都算，距离决定全食、偏食或环食。

branches.en: BLOCKING AND BEATING: the physical act becomes a figure for being outshone.
branches.cn: 遮挡与胜过：物理动作变成被比下去的修辞。

branches.en: TIME DARK AND TIME CYCLIC: favour goes dark, while eclipses return on schedule.
branches.cn: 变暗的时间与循环的时间：声望暗下去，而食按期回来。

branches.en: INVISIBLE BUT PRESENT: virology borrows the same dark interval.
branches.cn: 不可见却在场：病毒学借用了同一段黑暗间隔。

intro.en: Eclipse is a Greek compound with a prefix, a verb root and a noun ending; Latin and French carried it to English.
intro.cn: eclipse 是希腊复合词，含一个前缀、一个动词词根与一个名词词尾；经拉丁语与法语传入英语。

latinIntro.en: Latin eclipsis is a straight borrowing of the Greek noun; Latin also said defectus solis, 'failure of the sun', for the same event.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 eclipsis 是对希腊名词的直接借入；拉丁也用 defectus solis「太阳的缺失」指同一事件。

items.example: The prefix marks a going out or a failing.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀标记向外或缺失。

items.example: The root is shared with Latin linquere.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根与拉丁 linquere 共享。

items.example: The ending makes a noun of the verb.
items.exampleCN: 这个词尾把动词变成名词。

items.example: The sun went into eclipse.
items.exampleCN: 太阳进入了食。

items.example: Annular eclipses are rare here.
items.exampleCN: 环食在此地很少见。

items.example: The earlier record was eclipsed.
items.exampleCN: 早先的纪录被打破了。

items.example: An eclipsing binary dims twice a month.
items.exampleCN: 食双星每月变暗两次。

items.example: Eclipses happen near the ecliptic.
items.exampleCN: 食发生在黄道附近。

latinEntries.structure: eclipsis, eclipsis (f., third declension; from Greek)

latinEntries.meaning: failure, disappearance; used of an eclipsed sun
latinEntries.meaningCN: 缺失；消失；用于指被食的太阳
